english: Cacapon is a Shawnee name meaning “medicine water.” This shallow river winds among the Appalachian ridges to meet the Potomac. Its headwaters, near Mathias, are known as the Lost River: the stream disappears underground at the Sinks and reappears near Wardensville as the Cacapon. Farther downstream it receives the North River, its largest tributary, before continuing through the mountain valleys.
simp_chinese: 卡卡蓬是肖尼语名称，意为“药水”。这条浅河在阿巴拉契亚山脉之间蜿蜒，最终汇入波托马克河。马赛厄斯附近的上游称为失踪河：水流在辛克斯潜入地下，又在沃登斯维尔附近重新出现，成为卡卡蓬河。河水向下游接纳最大的支流北河，继续穿过山间谷地。

english: Cakaulevu, the Great Sea Reef, stretches along the northern shore of Vanua Levu in Fiji. Together with the neighbouring Pascoe Reef, this long barrier of coral extends for about two hundred kilometres. Its shallow waters and reefs form a distinct boundary between Vanua Levu's coast and the open sea.
simp_chinese: 卡考勒武又称大海礁，沿斐济瓦努阿岛北岸延伸。这道绵长的珊瑚堡礁与邻近的帕斯科礁合计长约二百公里。浅水与礁体在瓦努阿岛海岸和外海之间形成一道鲜明的界线。

english: Cakaulevu, the Great Sea Reef, lies off the northern shore of Vanua Levu. Its long barrier encloses channels and reefs in waters used by Fijian communities. Early in the nineteenth century sandalwood from Vanua Levu drew trading ships to Bua Bay on the island’s western side.
simp_chinese: 卡考莱武大海礁位于瓦努阿岛北岸外。漫长的堡礁围出水道和礁区，斐济社群使用这些水域。十九世纪初，瓦努阿岛的檀香吸引商船来到岛屿西侧的布阿湾。

english: The Cacaxtle were an Indigenous people of the southern Texas and northeastern Mexican borderlands. Their range took in the country from the Nueces River south across the Rio Grande. Their name refers to a netted frame used to carry loads on the back. Between 1653 and 1663 the Cacaxtle and their allies repeatedly attacked Spanish frontier settlements in Coahuila and Nuevo León. Spanish expeditions crossed the Rio Grande in 1663 and 1665 and fought two decisive battles, in which about two hundred Cacaxtle were killed and about as many captured. The captives were sold into slavery and put to work in the mines of Chihuahua and Zacatecas. After these campaigns the name rarely appears in the records.
simp_chinese: 卡卡斯特莱人是得克萨斯南部与墨西哥东北部边境地带的原住民。其活动范围从努埃塞斯河向南跨越格兰德河。族名指一种用于背负货物的网状背架。1653至1663年间，卡卡斯特莱人与盟友多次袭击科阿韦拉和新莱昂的西班牙边疆聚落。1663年和1665年，西班牙远征队越过格兰德河，在两次决定性战役中击杀约两百名卡卡斯特莱人，又俘虏了大致相同数量的人。俘虏被卖为奴隶，送往奇瓦瓦和萨卡特卡斯的矿山劳动。此后这一名称在记载中极少出现。

english:
Cacequi occupies open grassland between low ridges and shallow river valleys in western Rio Grande do Sul. Indigenous peoples long used these pampas before European settlement, exploiting game, fish, wild fruits and seasonal water while moving with the herds. The local Tupi-derived name was long preserved even as the population and political order changed.

The grasslands became a contested borderland between Portugal and Spain during the eighteenth century. The Treaty of Madrid in 1750 placed the Missions east of the Uruguay River under Portuguese rule, but warfare and the Treaty of Santo Ildefonso in 1777 reversed parts of the arrangement. Mission communities, cattle ranchers and military expeditions competed for land, water and routes across the pampas.

Portuguese forces occupied the eastern Missions in 1801, extending Rio Grande do Sul into the region around Cacequi. Cattle ranching spread across the natural pasture, linking the district to the charque trade and to routes toward the Uruguay frontier. Forts and military commands sought to protect ranches and regulate movement between Brazilian and Spanish territories. Estates and small settlements replaced the older mobility of Indigenous groups, while the remembered chief’s water survived in the place name.

The later city of Rivera lies here.
simp_chinese:
卡塞基位于南里奥格兰德州西部低丘与浅河谷之间的开阔草原。在欧洲殖民以前，原住民族利用这片潘帕斯，猎取野兽、捕鱼、采集野果并随兽群追逐季节性水源。后来形成的图皮语地名，在人口与政治秩序改变后仍被保存下来。

十八世纪，草原成为葡萄牙与西班牙争夺的边境。1750年《马德里条约》把乌拉圭河以东的传教区划归葡萄牙，但战争和1777年的《圣伊尔德丰索条约》又改变了部分安排。传教区社群、养牛者和军事远征队争夺土地、水源及横贯草原的通道。

1801年，葡萄牙军队占领东岸传教区，把南里奥格兰德州的范围推进到卡塞基一带。养牛业在天然牧场上扩展，使地方同腌肉贸易及通往乌拉圭边境的道路相连。要塞和军事据点试图保护庄园，并管控巴西与西班牙属地之间的往来。庄园和较小聚落取代原住民原有的流动生活，而关于首领水源的记忆仍留在地名之中。

后来的里韦拉即位于此地。

english:
Cáceres sits on a hill at the foot of the Sierra de la Mosca, beside the Roman road later called the Vía de la Plata. The Romans planted the colony of Norba Caesarina here; after the Visigoths wrecked it, the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mumin refounded the town in 1147 as a military base against the Christian north, and the Tower of Bujaco dates from this Muslim period. Alfonso IX of León took Cáceres on 23 April 1229.

His charter made it a royal town with only its own council, and its ban on lordly estates kept a strong high nobility from forming; the town was run instead by a middle rank of landholding knights. In the fifteenth century those families fought one another so fiercely that Isabella, staying here in 1477 during the war of the Castilian succession, made the twelve councillors permanent in an effort to calm them. Cáceres also had a sizeable Jewish quarter around San Antonio, with at least two synagogues, and about 140 Jewish families lived among a population of roughly 2,000 until the expulsion of 1492. The town remained rural until the eighteenth century, when a small bourgeoisie of stockmen and merchants settled as the sheep migrations declined; the Royal Audience of Extremadura was seated here in 1790, and Cáceres became capital of its province in 1822.
simp_chinese:
卡塞雷斯坐落在拉莫斯卡山脉脚下的一座山丘上，旁边是后来被称为白银之路的罗马古道。罗马人在此建立了诺尔瓦·凯撒里纳殖民地；西哥特人毁掉它之后，穆瓦希德哈里发阿卜杜勒·穆明在1147年重建此城，作为对付北方基督教国家的军事基地，布哈科塔就建于这一穆斯林时期。1229年4月23日，莱昂的阿方索九世攻取卡塞雷斯。

他颁给的特许状使卡塞雷斯成为只有自己市议会的王室城镇，禁止领主占有土地，也就没有形成强大的大贵族，城镇由一批拥有土地的骑士阶层管理。15世纪这些家族相互争斗激烈，伊莎贝拉1477年在卡斯蒂利亚王位继承战争期间驻留此地，把十二名市政议员定为终身职，以平息纷争。卡塞雷斯在圣安东尼奥一带还有相当规模的犹太区，至少有两座犹太会堂，在人口约两千的城里有大约140户犹太家庭，直到1492年被驱逐。直到18世纪，卡塞雷斯仍是乡村城镇，随着羊群迁徙业衰落，一批牧场主和商人组成的小资产阶级迁入；1790年，埃斯特雷马杜拉王家法院设在这里，1822年卡塞雷斯成为同名省份的省会。

english:
Cachamay lies on the lower Caroní River near its meeting with the Orinoco. Here the dark waters of the Caroní pass through rocky channels and cascades before joining the larger river. Forested islands divide the current around the falls. The confluence links the rivers descending from the Guiana highlands with the Orinoco, whose broad course continues east towards its Atlantic delta.

The later city of Ciudad Guayana lies here.
simp_chinese:
卡查迈位于卡罗尼河下游，靠近它与奥里诺科河的交汇处。深色的卡罗尼河水在汇入大河前穿过岩石水道与瀑布，林木覆盖的岛屿将水流分开。这一汇合处把圭亚那高地下来的河流接入奥里诺科河；后者继续向东流往大西洋三角洲。

后来的圭亚那城即位于此地。

english: Cacheu stands on the river of the same name, upstream from its Atlantic estuary. African and Luso-African merchants made it an important meeting point of the coastal and inland trading networks of Upper Guinea. In 1588 Manuel Lopes Cardoso fortified the settlement with the permission of a local ruler. Cacheu became a major port in the Atlantic trade in enslaved people. Portuguese companies sought to control its commerce in the seventeenth century, while local rulers and merchants continued to exercise power beyond the fort.
simp_chinese: 卡谢乌坐落在同名河流上，位于大西洋河口上游。非洲商人与葡非混血商人使它成为上几内亚沿海和内陆贸易网络的重要交汇点。1588年，曼努埃尔·洛佩斯·卡尔多佐经当地统治者许可，为聚落修建防御设施。卡谢乌成为大西洋奴隶贸易的重要港口。十七世纪，葡萄牙公司试图控制这里的商业，地方统治者与商人则继续在堡垒之外行使权力。

english: The Cachopostales were an Indigenous group of southern Texas, reported with the Pampopa along the Nueces and Frio rivers. Their homeland lay between the Rio Grande and the settlements of the San Antonio area, in a country of rivers and thorny brush. They may have been the same people later recorded as Postitos at San José y San Miguel de Aguayo mission, where people of that name were closely associated with the Pampopa during the eighteenth century.
simp_chinese: 卡乔波斯塔莱斯人是得克萨斯南部的原住民，据记载曾与潘波帕人共同生活在努埃塞斯河和弗里奥河沿岸。其故土位于格兰德河与圣安东尼奥地区聚落之间，河流与荆棘灌丛遍布。后来圣何塞－圣米格尔·德·阿瓜约传教区记录的波斯蒂托人可能与他们是同一群体；十八世纪，这些人与潘波帕人联系密切。

english: Caconda lies on the highland plateau of southern Angola, inland from the coast at Benguela, in the country of the Ovimbundu. The small kingdoms of this plateau, among them the M'Balundu, lived by farming and kept chickens, goats and pigs, adding a few cattle bought from the Nyaneka-Nkhumbi and Ovambo herders to the south. After the Portuguese settled at Benguela in the sixteenth century, caravans carried wax, honey and ivory down from the Chokwe, Luvale and Mbunda lands in the east, and the highland chiefs took a share of that trade, which also included slaves.
simp_chinese: 卡孔达位于安哥拉南部的高原上，从沿海的本格拉向内陆深入，属于奥温本杜人的地域。这片高原上的小王国（姆巴伦杜是其中之一）以农耕为生，饲养鸡、山羊和猪，并向南方的尼亚内卡-恩昆比和奥万博牧民购入少量牛只。16世纪葡萄牙人在本格拉定居后，商队把蜡、蜂蜜和象牙从东面的乔奎、卢瓦勒和姆本达人地区运下来，高原上的首领们也分得这条商路的一份利益，奴隶同样在交易之列。

english: Off the coast near Mogadishu, the Indian Ocean meets a shore of beaches and rocky points. The city grew as a centre of commerce, receiving ships from Arabia and India and gathering goods from the African interior. In the fourteenth century the traveller Ibn Battuta described a prosperous Muslim port with a Somali ruler. Seasonal winds brought ships to the coast and helped determine their return voyages.
simp_chinese: 摩加迪沙附近，印度洋与沙滩和岩石岬角构成的海岸相接。城镇发展为商业中心，接待来自阿拉伯和印度的船只，也汇集非洲内陆货物。14世纪旅行家伊本·白图泰记述了一座繁荣的穆斯林港口，由索马里统治者治理。季节风把船只带到海岸，也影响返航时间。

english:
Cadegomo lies in a desert valley of the Baja California peninsula, where springs and an intermittent watercourse support an oasis among dry mountains. The place was inhabited by Indigenous people before Spanish missionaries established a settlement there. Its water and cultivable ground made it valuable to the missions that spread through the peninsula in the eighteenth century.

In 1685 Isidro de Atondo y Antillón and the missionary Eusebio Francisco Kino explored this region during an early Spanish expedition. The Jesuit Nicolás Tamaral founded the mission of La Purísima Concepción de Cadegomó in 1720. Like other missions of the peninsula, it sought to gather Indigenous families around a church and cultivated lands, while relying on supplies brought from across the Gulf of California.
simp_chinese:
卡德戈莫位于下加利福尼亚半岛的沙漠山谷，泉水与间歇性水道在干山之间滋养出一片绿洲。西班牙传教士建立聚落之前，原住民已生活于此。水源和可耕地使它在十八世纪扩展的半岛传教网络中具有重要价值。

1685年，伊西德罗·德·阿通多－安蒂永与传教士埃乌塞维奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺在早期西班牙远征中考察这一地区。1720年，耶稣会士尼古拉斯·塔马拉尔建立卡德戈莫圣母无染原罪传教区。与半岛其他传教区一样，它试图将原住民家庭集中在教堂和耕地周围，同时依赖从加利福尼亚湾对岸运来的补给。

english:
Cadereyta stands in the semi-arid country south of the Sierra Gorda, where valleys give way to rugged mountains. The region was home to Otomí communities and Chichimeca peoples, including the Pames and Jonaces. Its position at the edge of the mountains made it a base for Spanish efforts to extend colonial authority into the Sierra Gorda.

Captain Alonso de Tovar founded the villa of Cadereyta in 1640 in the valley of San Nicolás de Tolentino. Its early population included Spaniards, Otomí people, Christianized Chichimecas, Africans and people of mixed ancestry. Land grants followed around the new settlement, while missionaries sought to establish a religious presence among the peoples of the mountains. In time Cadereyta became the seat of a wider colonial jurisdiction reaching into the Sierra Gorda.
simp_chinese:
卡德雷塔位于马德雷戈尔达山脉以南的半干旱地带，谷地在此逐渐让位于崎岖群山。这一地区有奥托米社群和奇奇梅卡诸族，包括帕梅人与霍纳塞人。山麓的位置使这里成为西班牙人向山中扩展殖民统治的据点。

1640年，阿隆索·德·托瓦尔上尉在圣尼古拉斯德托伦蒂诺谷地建立卡德雷塔镇。早期居民包括西班牙人、奥托米人、皈依基督教的奇奇梅卡人、非洲人及混血居民。新聚落周围随后分配土地，传教士也设法在山地各族中建立宗教据点。卡德雷塔后来成为辖区广及马德雷戈尔达山区的殖民行政中心。

english:
Settled around 1100 BC by Phoenicians from Tyre as #italic Gadir#!, the Strong Place, on a long sandbar reaching out into the Atlantic from the southern Iberian coast, Cádiz is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in western Europe, its harbor having welcomed Phoenician, Carthaginian, Roman, Visigoth, and Moorish fleets across three thousand years. The Romans called it #italic Gades#! and made it one of the wealthiest cities of their western empire, the home of poets, senators, and the celebrated dancing girls of the imperial period, but the long decline of late antiquity reduced it to a modest fishing town by the time the Moors held it. Captured by Alfonso X the Wise in 1262 and resettled as a Castilian frontier port, Cádiz in the early 14th century served as a major southern outlet of the Castilian realm, its Atlantic-facing harbor striving toward the wider ocean beyond.

The ocean the harbor looked toward soon came to it. Columbus sailed from Cádiz on his second and fourth voyages, the city became a home port of the treasure fleets, and that made it a target. In April 1587 Francis Drake held the harbor for three days and took or destroyed thirty-seven ships, delaying the Armada by a year; in 1596 an Anglo-Dutch fleet under the Earls of Essex and Nottingham captured the city itself, and when the crown refused a ransom they burned much of it before sailing away. Cádiz rose again in the 18th century, after the Casa de Contratación moved here from Seville in 1717 and the city held the trade of the Americas almost alone until 1778. Its proudest hour came in the war against Napoleon. Cádiz was one of the few Spanish cities the French never took, and the Cortes that sat behind its walls proclaimed here the liberal Constitution of 1812.
simp_chinese:
加的斯由推罗的腓尼基人在约公元前1100年建立，名为#italic 加迪尔#!，意为“坚固之地”。它坐落在从伊比利亚半岛南部海岸延伸至大西洋的一条长长的沙洲上，是西欧最古老的持续有人居住的城市之一。三千年来，其港口接待过腓尼基人、迦太基人、罗马人、西哥特人和摩尔人的船队。罗马人称其为#italic 加德斯#!，在他们治理下，加的斯成为西罗马帝国最富庶的城市之一，是诗人、元老以及帝国时期著名舞女的故乡。然而，古典时代晚期的长期衰落，使摩尔人统治时它已沦为一座普通的渔镇。1262年，“智者”阿方索十世将其收复，并迁入居民建立为卡斯蒂利亚的边境港口。至14世纪初，加的斯已成为卡斯蒂利亚王国南部最主要的出海口之一，其面向大西洋的港口已开始将目光投向更广阔的海洋。

港口原本眺望的那片大洋，很快就来到了它面前。哥伦布第二次和第四次远航都从加的斯出发，这里成了运宝船队的母港，也因此成为敌人的目标。1587年4月，弗朗西斯·德雷克占领港口三天，俘获或击毁三十七艘船只，使无敌舰队的出航推迟了一年；1596年，埃塞克斯伯爵和诺丁汉伯爵率领的英荷联合舰队攻下城市，王室拒付赎金，他们临走前放火烧毁了大半个城。18世纪加的斯重新崛起：1717年，掌管美洲贸易的贸易署从塞维利亚迁来，此后直到1778年，对美洲的贸易几乎由它独揽。它最光荣的时刻出现在抗击拿破仑的战争中。加的斯是法军始终未能攻下的少数西班牙城市之一，困守城中的议会在这里颁布了自由主义的1812年宪法。

english:
Caen lies on the Orne and the Odon, a short distance inland from the Norman coast. Around 1060 William the Conqueror began the great castle above the town, and he and his wife Matilda of Flanders founded the two abbeys that flank the town, the Abbaye aux Hommes and the Abbaye aux Dames, where each was buried. The pale local limestone, known as Caen stone, was shipped across the Channel to build English cathedrals and castles. At Christmas 1182 Henry II held a court in the castle's hall with Richard the Lionheart, John and more than a thousand knights.

Philip II of France took Caen in 1204. On 26 July 1346 Edward III's army stormed the town in less than a day, killing some three thousand people and burning the merchants' quarter on the Île Saint-Jean; only the castle held out. Henry V besieged Caen in 1417 and carried it by assault, and in 1432 John of Lancaster, Duke of Bedford, regent for Henry VI, founded the university here. French troops recovered the town in 1450. In July 1793 Girondin deputies fleeing Paris tried to raise Normandy against the Convention from Caen, and Charlotte Corday left the city to assassinate Marat.
simp_chinese:
卡昂位于奥恩河与奥东河畔，距诺曼底海岸不远。约1060年，征服者威廉开始在城镇上方修建大城堡，他与妻子佛兰德的玛蒂尔达还创建了分立城区两侧的男修院和女修院，两人分别安葬其中。当地浅色石灰岩即“卡昂石”被运过海峡，用来建造英格兰的大教堂和城堡。1182年圣诞节，亨利二世在城堡大厅举行朝会，理查、约翰和一千多名骑士出席。

1204年，法王腓力二世夺取卡昂。1346年7月26日，爱德华三世的军队不到一天就攻下全城，杀死约三千人，并烧毁圣让岛上的商人区，只有城堡守住。1417年亨利五世围攻卡昂并强攻得手，1432年，亨利六世的摄政、贝德福德公爵兰开斯特的约翰在此创办大学。1450年，法军收复该城。1793年7月，逃出巴黎的吉伦特派议员以卡昂为基地，试图发动诺曼底反对国民公会，夏洛特·科黛则从这里出发去刺杀马拉。

english:
Home to the highest-quality coal in Europe, the Welsh Valleys became a center for iron-making in the latter half of the 18th century.

Long before coal and iron, Caerphilly meant its castle: the fortress Gilbert de Clare had raised in the Rhymney valley from 1268, ringed by artificial lakes, with a small town at its gate. In January 1316 Llywelyn Bren, the Welsh lord of Senghenydd, rose against the royal officials holding the de Clare lands; his men could not break the inner defences, but they burned the town before a royal army defeated him on Caerphilly Mountain. Ten years later Edward II and Hugh le Despenser took refuge in the castle as Queen Isabella's forces closed in, and after the two had fled, its garrison held out until March 1327.

After 1486 the castle declined, eclipsed by Cardiff, and once its sluice-gates failed the lakes probably drained away. When John Leland came about 1539 he found a ruin standing in marshland, with a single tower used as a prison, and from 1583 its tenant Thomas Lewis carried off its stone to enlarge his own house. The town beside it lived on, growing into a market town in the 18th century, and in 1776 the ruins passed to the Marquesses of Bute.
simp_chinese:
威尔士山谷拥有欧洲最高品质的煤矿，在18世纪后半叶成为炼铁业中心。

在煤和铁之前，卡菲利出名的是城堡。这座要塞由吉尔伯特·德·克莱尔从1268年起在里姆尼河谷修建，四周环绕人工湖，城门外有一座小镇。1316年1月，森根尼德的威尔士领主卢埃林·布伦起兵反抗掌管德·克莱尔领地的王室官员；他的人马攻不破内层防御，却把小镇烧了，随后王室军队在卡菲利山击败了他。十年后，王后伊莎贝拉的军队步步逼近，爱德华二世和小休·德斯潘塞躲进城堡；两人出逃后，守军仍坚守到1327年3月。

1486年以后，城堡被卡迪夫的风头盖过，日渐衰落，水闸失修后湖水大概也慢慢流干了。约1539年约翰·利兰来时，城堡已是沼泽中的一片废墟，只有一座塔还被用作监狱；1583年起，租下城堡的托马斯·刘易斯拆走石料，扩建自己的宅邸。城堡旁的小镇却延续下来，18世纪成长为集镇；1776年，这片废墟归入比特侯爵家族名下。

english: The Caeté were a Tupi-speaking people whose lands extended along the northeastern Brazilian coast toward the mouth of the São Francisco. Portuguese expansion brought violent conflict to their country. After Bishop Pero Fernandes Sardinha died following a shipwreck in 1556, colonial authorities declared a “just war” against the Caeté; expeditions attacked their communities, and many people were enslaved or driven from their lands.
simp_chinese: 卡埃特人操图皮语，其土地沿巴西东北海岸延伸至圣弗朗西斯科河口一带。葡萄牙人的扩张给他们的家园带来了激烈冲突。1556年，主教佩罗·费尔南德斯·萨尔迪尼亚在船只失事后遇害；殖民当局随后宣布对卡埃特人发动“正义战争”。远征队袭击他们的村落，许多人遭到奴役或被迫离开土地。

english: The Caeté estuary opens to the Atlantic on the coast of Pará, near Bragança. Mangroves cover the peninsula beside the river, where tidal channels connect the forest to the estuary and neighbouring bays. Among their roots lives the uçá crab, which digs burrows in the mud and provides food for people along the Caeté.
simp_chinese: 卡埃特河口在帕拉海岸向大西洋敞开，靠近布拉干萨。红树林覆盖河边的半岛，潮汐水道将林地与河口及邻近海湾相连。红树根间生活着乌萨蟹，它们在泥中挖洞，也是卡埃特河沿岸居民的食物来源。

english:
Caeté lies among the wooded hills of Minas Gerais, in a region opened to colonial mining at the end of the seventeenth century. Gold drew prospectors from São Paulo and elsewhere, and rivalry over the new workings helped provoke the War of the Emboabas. After the fighting, the settlement grew under Portuguese administration and became Vila Nova da Rainha do Caeté in 1714.

The later city of Belo Horizonte lies here.
simp_chinese:
卡埃特位于米纳斯吉拉斯林木覆盖的丘陵之间，十七世纪末殖民者开始在这一地区采矿。黄金吸引了来自圣保罗和其他地方的寻矿者，争夺新矿场的竞争促成了恩博阿巴斯战争。战斗结束后，聚落在葡萄牙统治下发展，于1714年成为卡埃特王后新镇。

后来的贝洛奥里藏特即位于此地。

english: Caftacha lies west of the headwaters of the Pearl River. In the hills to the southeast stands Nanih Waiya, an ancient earthen mound important to Choctaw accounts of their origins. Traditions also associate a nearby cave with the emergence of the people. Nanih Waiya Creek joins other streams that form the Pearl, which winds south through Mississippi toward the Gulf of Mexico.
simp_chinese: 卡夫塔查位于珀尔河源区以西。东南方丘陵中有古老土丘纳尼怀亚，它在乔克托人的起源叙述中占有重要地位；传统也将附近洞穴与族人的诞生相联系。纳尼怀亚溪与其他溪流共同形成珀尔河，河水蜿蜒穿过密西西比，向南流往墨西哥湾。

english: Cagayan de Sulu, known to its inhabitants as Mapun, lies in the Sulu Sea near northern Borneo and Palawan. The island and its neighbouring islets are home to the Jama Mapun, a Sama-speaking people whose connections extend across nearby islands and coasts. Mapun's relationship with the Sultanate of Sulu linked it to Jolo farther east.
simp_chinese: 苏禄卡加延岛被当地居民称为马蓬，位于苏禄海中，靠近婆罗洲北部与巴拉望。岛屿及附近小岛是讲萨马语的贾马马蓬人的家园，他们的联系遍及邻近岛屿和海岸。马蓬与苏禄苏丹国的关系，也将其与更东面的霍洛联系起来。

english: Cagayancillo lies in the Sulu Sea between Palawan and the Visayan Islands. The low islands and reefs of this small group rise from waters far from the larger shores around them. To the southwest lie the Tubbataha reefs, coral atolls whose waters nurture fish and other marine life in the surrounding sea.
simp_chinese: 卡加延西略位于苏禄海中，介于巴拉望与维萨亚斯群岛之间。这一小群岛的低平岛屿和礁石从海中升起，远离周围较大的陆地。西南方是图巴塔哈珊瑚环礁，其水域孕育鱼类和其他海洋生物，丰富了周围海域。

english:
Cagliari stands above a sheltered harbour on the southern coast of Sardinia. The fortified hill of Castello overlooks the port, while the Campidano plain and the mineral lands to the west supplied the city with grain and ores. Carthaginian and Roman remains bear witness to its long history as a Mediterranean centre.

After the Aragonese conquest in the fourteenth century, Cagliari became the seat of royal government in Sardinia. A viceroy governed from the royal palace, and the fortifications were strengthened with bastions in the sixteenth century. The House of Savoy gained the island in the eighteenth century. In 1793 the inhabitants helped repel a French attack; the following year resentment at Savoyard rule led them to expel the viceroy and Piedmontese officials, though Savoy later recovered control.
simp_chinese:
卡利亚里俯瞰撒丁岛南岸的一处避风港。设防的卡斯泰洛高地俯视港口，坎皮达诺平原和西方矿区为城市提供谷物与矿石。迦太基和罗马遗迹见证了它作为地中海中心的漫长历史。

十四世纪阿拉贡征服后，卡利亚里成为撒丁王国的政府驻地。总督在王宫治理岛屿，十六世纪城防又以棱堡加强。十八世纪，萨伏依家族取得撒丁岛。1793年，居民帮助击退法国进攻；次年，对萨伏依统治的不满促使他们驱逐总督和皮埃蒙特官员，但萨伏依后来恢复了控制。

english: The Caguán rises on the eastern slopes of the Colombian Andes and flows down into the humid forests of the Amazonian lowlands. Its waters join the Caquetá, part of the great Amazon river system. The lower Caguán was home to Indigenous peoples including the Carijona and Coreguaje. Forested banks and tributaries frame a waterway that links the Andean foothills with the broad rivers farther downstream.
simp_chinese: 卡关河发源于哥伦比亚安第斯山脉东坡，向下流入亚马孙低地的湿润森林，最终汇入属于亚马孙水系的卡克塔河。卡关河下游曾是卡里霍纳和科雷瓜赫等原住民族的家园。林木覆盖的河岸与支流环绕水道，将安第斯山麓与下游更宽阔的河流连接起来。

english: Near the Tres Montes peninsula, Caguatl faces the stormy approaches to the Gulf of Penas. The peninsula projects southward from Taitao into a maze of inlets and islands. Chono seafarers travelled by canoe through the archipelagos as far south as Taitao and the gulf. In 1741 the British ship Wager was wrecked farther south during a storm, revealing how dangerous this exposed passage could be to sailing vessels.
simp_chinese: 卡瓜特尔靠近特雷斯蒙特斯半岛，面向通往佩纳斯湾的风暴海域。半岛从泰陶向南伸出，附近港湾与岛屿交错。乔诺人乘舟穿行于群岛之间，活动范围向南延伸至泰陶与佩纳斯湾。1741年，英国“韦杰”号在更南方遭遇风暴而失事，显出这条暴露航路对帆船的危险。

english: Cayuga Lake stretches north and south through a deep basin carved by glaciers, one of the long Finger Lakes of the northeastern interior. Its waters drain northward toward the Seneca River and Lake Ontario. The lake and its shores were home to Cayuga villages, between the lands of their Onondaga and Seneca neighbours. The Cayuga were one of the founding nations of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, whose council joined the peoples of the longhouse.
simp_chinese: 卡尤加湖南北延伸，位于冰川凿出的深邃盆地中，是北美东北内陆狭长的五指湖之一。湖水向北流往塞内卡河和安大略湖。卡尤加人的村落分布在湖畔，东面是奥农达加人的土地，西面是塞内卡人的土地。卡尤加人是霍迪诺肖尼联盟的创始成员之一，联盟议会将这些“长屋之民”联系起来。

english:
Cahama lies on the dry plateau of southwestern Angola, a short way north of the Cunene River, where open woodland and thorny scrub give way to the semi-desert of the Namib fringe. Rain is scarce and uneven, and the land is better suited to cattle than to crops.

This was the country of Bantu-speaking herders, among them Herero-related groups who had moved into the south-west of Africa from the east by about the fifteenth century. Their wealth was cattle, and homesteads shifted with the grazing and the water holes. Settlement stayed scattered, and the Cunene, flowing out of the Angolan highlands toward the Atlantic, was the one dependable water line in a wide dry land.
simp_chinese:
卡哈马位于安哥拉西南部的干旱高原上，在库内内河以北不远处，开阔林地和多刺灌丛在这里逐渐过渡为纳米布边缘的半荒漠。降雨稀少且不均，土地更适合养牛而不是种庄稼。

这里是讲班图语的牧民之地，其中有与赫雷罗人相近的群体，约在十五世纪前后从东方迁入非洲西南部。他们的财富是牛群，住所随牧场和水塘迁移。聚落始终分散，自安哥拉高地流向大西洋的库内内河，是这片辽阔干旱土地上唯一可靠的水线。

english: Cahay was an Indigenous district of Xaragua on western Hispaniola. Bartolomé de las Casas described villages along this coast, a short journey from Xaragua, whose inhabitants cultivated crops including sweet potatoes and yams. The district appears in accounts of the turbulent years following the Spanish arrival, when Alonso de Ojeda’s men came ashore and took provisions by force. Its name preserves a part of the island’s Taíno geography.
simp_chinese: 卡海是伊斯帕尼奥拉西部哈拉瓜的原住民地区。巴托洛梅·德拉斯卡萨斯描述了这片距哈拉瓜不远的海岸村落，居民种植甘薯和薯蓣等作物。西班牙人到来后局势动荡的记载中出现了这个地区：阿隆索·德·奥赫达的部下曾上岸强取粮食。卡海之名保留了岛屿泰诺地理的一部分。

english: Cahe is the Assiniboine name for Wood Mountain, an upland rising above the prairie of southern Saskatchewan. Its wooded slopes stand out against the surrounding grasslands, with the broken country of the Big Muddy to the southeast. The Wood Mountain people, a band of the Assiniboine, lived in this wider region and maintained close ties with the Assiniboine of the Cypress Hills to the west.
simp_chinese: 卡赫是伍德山的阿西尼博因语名称。这片高地耸立于萨斯喀彻温南部的草原之上，林木覆盖的山坡在周围草地中格外醒目；东南方则是大泥河的崎岖恶地。阿西尼博因人的伍德山支群生活在这一带，与西方赛普拉斯丘陵的阿西尼博因人关系密切。

english: Cahenda was one of the Dembos chiefdoms in the hills northeast of Luanda. Its rulers governed Kimbundu-speaking communities amid the competing claims of Kongo, Matamba and Portuguese Angola. During the late seventeenth century Cahenda grew in influence as nearby Mbwila weakened. In 1686 its ruler used support from Angola to take over the neighbouring polity of Mutemo a Kinjenga. Written correspondence became part of the political life of Cahenda's rulers as they dealt with other powers.
simp_chinese: 卡亨达是罗安达东北丘陵地区登博斯诸酋邦之一。其统治者治理操金本杜语的社区，同时应对刚果、马坦巴和葡属安哥拉等势力的竞争。十七世纪末，邻近的姆布维拉衰落，卡亨达的影响逐渐增长。1686年，卡亨达统治者借助安哥拉的支持，夺取了邻近的穆特马·阿金金加政权。在与其他势力交往时，书面通信也成为卡亨达统治者政治生活的一部分。

english:
Cahiagué was a major Wendat village in the country north of Lake Simcoe. It belonged to the Arendarhonon, one of the peoples of the Wendat Confederacy, whose villages and fields occupied the lands between the lake and Georgian Bay. The village was a place of councils and gathering as well as a centre of the surrounding agricultural country.

In 1615 Samuel de Champlain visited Cahiagué after travelling through Wendake. There he joined Wendat allies preparing an expedition against the Onondaga, one of the Haudenosaunee nations south of Lake Ontario. The force crossed the lake and attacked a fortified village, but failed to take it. Later accounts describe Cahiagué's population declining and dividing into two settlements that were rebuilt elsewhere, a reminder that villages could move as communities and circumstances changed.
simp_chinese:
卡希亚格是锡姆科湖以北的一座重要温达特村庄，属于温达特联盟中的阿伦达罗农人。他们的村庄和田地分布在湖泊与乔治亚湾之间。卡希亚格既是周围农业地区的中心，也是举行议事与集会的地方。

1615年，萨缪尔·德·尚普兰穿行温达克后到访卡希亚格，在此加入温达特盟友准备的远征，目标是安大略湖南面的豪德诺索尼诸族之一奥农达加人。队伍渡湖攻击一座设防村庄，却未能攻下。后来的记载说卡希亚格人口减少，居民分成两个聚落并在别处重建，显示村庄会随着社群与环境的变化而迁移。

english:
Cahokia is the Mississippian city whose earthen mounds rise from the American Bottom, the floodplain of the Mississippi opposite the later town of St. Louis, close to where the Missouri and Illinois rivers meet. Around 1050 its builders laid out a planned city with a Grand Plaza and dozens of mounds, and by about 1100 it held perhaps 15,000 to 20,000 people, trading copper, shells and Mill Creek chert with the Great Lakes and the Gulf Coast. It was the largest urban centre north of Mexico, and its original name is unknown.

By 1337 the city was in its last decades. From the late twelfth century people had been leaving, a walled compound had burned around 1160, and a palisade built about 1175 was rebuilt again and again around a smaller core. By 1350 the city was abandoned, and Cahokians went south into the Cairo Lowlands and the Central Mississippi Valley. For two centuries the surrounding country stood nearly empty, in what scholars call the Vacant Quarter. In the mid-seventeenth century Algonquian-speaking people of the Illinois Confederation moved in, among them the Cahokia tribe that lent its name to the mounds. French families later claimed the land, and around 1809 Trappist monks lived on the grounds.
simp_chinese:
卡霍基亚是密西西比文化的城市，土丘耸立在美国低地，即密西西比河与后来的圣路易斯城隔河相对的冲积平原上，靠近密苏里河和伊利诺伊河的汇流处。约1050年，建城者规划出带有大广场和数十座土丘的城市，到约1100年，城里大概有一万五千到两万人，与五大湖地区和墨西哥湾沿岸交换铜、贝壳和米尔溪燧石。这是墨西哥以北最大的城市中心，它最初的名字已不可考。

到1337年，这座城市已近尾声。12世纪晚期起，人们陆续离开，约1160年一处有围墙的居住区被焚毁，约1175年修的木栅此后一再重建，围住的范围越来越小。1350年前后城市被放弃，卡霍基亚人南迁到开罗低地和密西西比河谷中部。此后两个世纪，周边地区几乎无人居住，被学者称为“空缺地带”。17世纪中叶，伊利诺伊联盟的阿尔衮琴语人群迁入，其中的卡霍基亚部落为土丘留下了名字。后来法国家庭圈占了这片土地，约1809年有特拉普派修士住在此地。

english:
Cahors occupies a peninsula enclosed by a great bend of the Lot. Bridges and river traffic sustained a prosperous town governed by its consuls alongside the authority of its bishop. The consuls began the fortified Valentré bridge in 1308, adding a third crossing to the medieval city. Its arches and towers guarded the western approach to the peninsula, where merchants and travellers crossed the broad river.

In 1332 Pope John XXII, a native of Cahors, founded a university in his home city. Its schools of law, theology and medicine added learning to the town's commercial and ecclesiastical importance. The bridge and the university alike testify to the ambitions of a city whose influence extended well beyond the confines of its river bend.
simp_chinese:
卡奥尔占据洛特河大河曲环抱的半岛。桥梁与河运支撑着这座繁荣的城镇，执政官与主教在此共掌权力。1308年，执政官开始修建设防的瓦朗特雷桥，为中世纪城市增添第三处渡河通道。桥上的拱券和塔楼守卫着半岛西侧的入口，商人与旅人在此渡河。

1332年，出生于卡奥尔的教宗若望二十二世在故乡创办大学，设立法律、神学和医学学科，使这座商业与教会中心增添了学术地位。桥梁与大学共同见证了城市的雄心，它的影响远远超出了河曲所围的土地。

english: Cahuachi was a great Nasca ceremonial center in the desert of southern Peru, overlooking the Nazca River valley. Its builders raised broad adobe platforms, truncated pyramids and plazas in a landscape where water was precious. People gathered there for ceremonies, bringing offerings and finely made textiles and pottery. Much of the complex was abandoned as a major center by the fourth century, long before the rise of the Inca Empire, leaving monumental earthen structures beside the valley.
simp_chinese: 卡瓦奇是秘鲁南部沙漠中的大型纳斯卡礼仪中心，俯瞰纳斯卡河谷。建造者在水源珍贵的地带修筑宽阔土坯台基、截顶金字塔和广场。人们聚集于此举行仪式，带来祭品、精美织物与陶器。到四世纪，这片建筑群大部分已不再作为主要中心使用，远早于印加帝国兴起；宏伟土建筑则留在谷地旁。

english:
Cahul lies in southern Bessarabia near the lower Prut. The settlement was recorded as Șcheia in 1502 and as Frumoasa in 1716, before receiving the name Cahul in memory of a major eighteenth-century battle fought in the surrounding district. Its position near the river and the Danube placed it in the lands contested by Moldavia, the Ottoman Empire and Russia over many generations.

In 1770, during the Russo-Turkish War, a Russian army under Pyotr Rumyantsev defeated a much larger Ottoman force at the Battle of Kagul. The settlement remained part of Moldavia until the Treaty of Bucharest in 1812 brought Bessarabia under Russian rule. Its successive names preserve both the older Moldavian village and the memory of the battle that made the district famous.
simp_chinese:
卡胡尔位于比萨拉比亚南部，靠近普鲁特河下游。这处聚落在1502年的记载中称为什凯亚，1716年称为弗鲁莫阿萨，后来为纪念附近的一场战役而得名卡胡尔。它所在的土地长期为摩尔达维亚、奥斯曼帝国和俄罗斯争夺。

1770年俄土战争期间，彼得·鲁缅采夫率领的俄军在卡古尔战役中击败了人数多得多的奥斯曼军队。此地仍属摩尔达维亚，直到1812年《布加勒斯特条约》使比萨拉比亚归入俄罗斯。聚落先后的名称既保留了古老摩尔达维亚村庄的记忆，也纪念了使这一地区闻名的战役。

english:
The southern Cayapó inhabited a wide region of central Brazil, including northern São Paulo and the neighbouring uplands of Goiás and Minas Gerais. They spoke Jê languages and occupied woodland, grasslands and river valleys before Portuguese expansion. In the eighteenth century mining routes, cattle estates and colonial expeditions brought warfare and pressure on their lands.

The later city of Ribeirão Preto lies here.
simp_chinese:
南卡亚波人居住在巴西中部广大地区，包括圣保罗北部和戈亚斯、米纳斯吉拉斯邻近高地。他们使用热语，在葡萄牙扩张之前居住于林地、草原和河谷。十八世纪，采矿道路、养牛庄园与殖民远征队带来了战争，使他们的土地受到压力。

后来的里贝朗普雷图即位于此地。

english:
Caicó lies beside the Seridó River in the dry interior of northeastern Brazil. Its landscape of seasonal watercourses and thorny vegetation was home to Indigenous peoples before Portuguese settlers advanced into the region with their cattle. The river gave its name to the wider Seridó country, whose inhabitants depended on its waters in a climate of irregular rain.

During the late seventeenth century the expansion of ranching brought violent conflict with Indigenous communities. A fortified house known as the Casa Forte do Cuó was built near the river in the 1680s as a base for colonial forces. Settlement grew around it, and by 1735 the place was recognised as the povoação of Caicó. Its early history was shaped by the contest for land and water in the sertão.
simp_chinese:
卡伊科位于巴西东北部干旱内陆的塞里多河畔。葡萄牙殖民者带着牛群进入之前，原住民族已居住在这片季节性水道与多刺植被遍布的土地上。河流也为更广阔的塞里多地区赋予了名称；降雨不规律，当地居民依赖河水生活。

十七世纪末，牧场扩张引发与原住民社区的激烈冲突。1680年代，殖民者在河边修建称为库奥堡屋的防御建筑，作为军队据点。聚落在其周围成长，到1735年已被称为卡伊科聚居地。它的早期历史深受塞尔唐土地与水源争夺的影响。

sources.title: CLÉRYSTON RAFAELL WANDERLEY DE MEDEIROS - DISSERTAÇÃO PPGH CH 2012.pdf

english: Caillou Lake lies among the coastal marshes of southern Louisiana, in a maze of shallow waters and bayous near Terrebonne Bay. Grand Bayou du Large connects the lake with Caillou Bay to the south. The low-lying country is shaped by the meeting of river waters, marsh vegetation and the Gulf. Its interconnected waterways run through the traditional homelands of Indigenous communities of the Louisiana coast, including peoples who lived along Bayou Terrebonne and Bayou Lafourche.
simp_chinese: 卡尤湖位于路易斯安那南部沿海湿地，处在泰勒博讷湾附近浅水与河汊交织的地区。大迪拉日河汊将湖泊与南面的卡尤湾相连。这片低洼土地由河水、湿地植物和墨西哥湾共同塑造。相互连接的水道穿过路易斯安那海岸原住民社群的传统家园，其中包括生活在泰勒博讷河汊和拉富尔什河汊沿岸的人群。

english:
Cairiani is associated with Trinidad, a large island close to the South American mainland. Its northern mountains, central plains and southern wetlands enclose a varied landscape of rivers and forests. Indigenous peoples had lived on the island for thousands of years before Spanish settlement, maintaining connections across the narrow waters to the nearby mainland.

In 1592 the Spanish founded San José de Oruña as their principal settlement. Indigenous communities were drawn into colonial systems of labor and mission life, while the island remained sparsely settled by Europeans for much of the period. During the late eighteenth century new European settlers and enslaved workers arrived as plantation agriculture expanded. A British naval expedition captured Trinidad in 1797, and Spain formally ceded it in 1802.

The later city of Port of Spain lies here.
simp_chinese:
凯里亚尼与靠近南美大陆的特立尼达岛有关。北部山脉、中部平原和南部湿地围出河流与森林交织的多样景观。西班牙定居之前，原住民已在岛上生活数千年，并通过狭窄海域与大陆保持联系。

1592年，西班牙人建立圣何塞德奥鲁尼亚作为主要聚落。原住民社群被纳入殖民劳动与传教制度，而欧洲人在很长时期内定居稀少。十八世纪末种植园农业扩张，新移民与被奴役的劳工陆续抵达。1797年英国远征军夺取特立尼达，西班牙于1802年正式割让该岛。

后来的西班牙港即位于此地。

english:
Cairngorm rises toward the eastern rim of the Scottish Highlands as a broad granite massif of high plateaus, corries and rounded summits. Cairn Gorm itself reaches 1,245 metres and looks over Strathspey; deeper in the range, Ben Macdui rises above it. Arctic-alpine vegetation, exposed tors and long-lasting snow patches mark a landscape where wind and sudden storms can close simple routes.

High passes linked the inhabited straths rather than crossing the summits. From the Middle Ages onward, herders and cattle drovers used tracks through the mountains to move stock between Speyside, Deeside and southern markets. Farmsteads and shielings occupied the lower glens, while cattle raiding made control of routes a matter of local power. The name Cairn Gorm comes from Scottish Gaelic An Càrn Gorm, the blue or green cairn.

By the eighteenth century the mountains formed a rugged interior between Highland communities and the growing towns of Moray. Drovers, soldiers and travelers crossed their passes, but the high ground remained thinly settled and difficult in winter. Cairngorm's place from the Middle Ages to the nineteenth century was therefore one of resource, pastoral movement and exposure rather than permanent upland settlement.
simp_chinese:
凯恩戈姆山位于苏格兰高地东缘，是一片由高台地、冰斗和浑圆山顶构成的广阔花岗岩山群。凯恩戈姆山本身高1245米，俯瞰斯佩谷；山群深处的本麦克杜伊峰还要更高。高山苔原植被、裸露岩块与长期积雪塑造了这里，大风和骤至的暴风雪常使简单路线中断。

较高的山口连接有人居住的河谷，人们通常绕过峰顶通行。中世纪以后，牧人和赶牛者利用穿山道路，把牲畜从斯佩谷、迪河谷运往南部市场。农庄与夏季牧棚分布在下部峡谷，牛群劫掠则让道路控制成为地方权力的一部分。凯恩戈姆之名源自苏格兰盖尔语，意为蓝灰色的石堆。

到十八世纪，山群仍是高地社群与马里新兴城镇之间的崎岖内陆。赶牛者、士兵和旅人穿行山口，高处却始终聚落稀少，冬季尤为艰险。凯恩戈姆在近代早期的面貌由牧业资源、牲畜移动和严酷暴露共同决定，而非永久性的高地定居。

english:
Founded in 969 by the Fatimid general Jawhar aṣ-Ṣiqillī beside the ancient Roman fortress of Babylon, Al-Qāhira, 'The Victorious', quickly supplanted Alexandria as the heart of Egypt. Under the Ayyubids and Mamluks it grew into the most populous city in the Islamic world, its markets and mosques drawing merchants, scholars, and pilgrims from across three continents. When the Mongols shattered Baghdad in 1258, Cairo stood as the uncontested capital of Islamic civilization, a city of extraordinary grandeur whose minarets rose above a river valley that had sustained human life since the dawn of history.

The city reached its height under the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, whose long reign ended in 1341: by then Cairo held close to half a million people, more than any city west of China. The Black Death broke that prosperity. Ibn Battuta, passing through again in 1348, heard of thousands dying in a single day, and the plague returned more than fifty times before 1517. Yet it was in these grim years that Sultan Hasan raised his madrasa-mosque below the Citadel, the largest monument of the Mamluk age.

The Ottomans, who had beaten the Mamluk army in Syria in 1516, took Egypt the next year and ruled it from Constantinople as a province, with Cairo as its capital. No longer on the spice route, the city's merchants found a new staple in Yemeni coffee, which they carried with Indian cloth to Anatolia, North Africa, and the Balkans, and Cairo stayed the second city of the empire. In the same centuries al-Azhar rose above every other school of the Islamic world, its fame carried home by the pilgrims who passed through on the road to Mecca.
simp_chinese:
公元969年，法蒂玛王朝的将军乔哈尔·萨基利在古罗马巴比伦堡垒旁建立了卡希拉——“胜利者之城”，它迅速取代亚历山大港成为了埃及的中心。在阿尤布王朝和马穆鲁克王朝统治下，开罗成长为伊斯兰世界人口最多的城市，其市场和清真寺吸引了来自三大洲的商人、学者和朝圣者。1258年蒙古人摧毁巴格达后，开罗作为伊斯兰文明无可争议的首都屹立不倒——这座宏伟非凡的城市，其宣礼塔高耸于一条自历史黎明之初便滋养着人类生命的河谷之上。

开罗的鼎盛在马穆鲁克苏丹纳西尔·穆罕默德治下到来，他漫长的统治于1341年结束时，城中人口已近五十万，中国以西没有一座城市比它更大。黑死病打断了这份繁荣。1348年伊本·白图泰再次途经开罗，听说一天就死去数千人；到1517年，瘟疫又来了五十多次。然而正是在这些阴暗的年月里，苏丹哈桑在城堡之下建起他的伊斯兰学校兼清真寺，那是马穆鲁克时代最大的建筑。

1516年在叙利亚击败马穆鲁克军队的奥斯曼人，次年征服埃及，从君士坦丁堡把它作为行省统治，开罗为省会。这座城市已不在香料商路上，开罗商人却找到了新的大宗货物：也门咖啡，他们把它和印度布匹一起运往安纳托利亚、北非和巴尔干，开罗也始终是帝国的第二大城市。同一时期，爱资哈尔在伊斯兰世界的学府中独占鳌头，途经此地前往麦加的朝圣者把它的名声带回了各地。

english:
Cairo Montenotte spreads along the left bank of the Bormida in the upper Val Bormida, inland from Savona and Genoa. It became the valley’s principal town despite having no outlet on the sea, its importance growing from passage through a landscape of hills rather than from a harbour. Finds of arrowheads, spearpoints and polished stone axes show Neolithic activity, and the area was probably occupied by the Ligurian Statielli before Rome conquered Liguria.

Roman engineers cut the Via Aemilia Scauri through the valley in 109 BC, linking Tortona with Vado Ligure; a station called Canalicum or Calanico stood at Cairo. Its name comes from a Ligurian root meaning stone or rock. “Carium” was first documented in 967, when Emperor Otto I granted lands devastated by earlier Lombard and Saracen incursions.

Cairo’s castle was later sold to Genoa, and the valley remained a contested route among regional lords. In 1796 Montenotte Superiore became the setting of Napoleon’s first success in the Italian campaign. That battle gave the town a wider military identity.
simp_chinese:
卡伊罗·蒙泰诺泰沿博尔米达河左岸展开，坐落在萨沃纳和热那亚内陆的上博尔米达谷。这里没有出海口，却发展为谷内主要城镇，其地位来自穿越丘陵的交通，而非港湾贸易。箭镞、矛尖和磨制石斧等发现表明新石器时代已有活动，罗马征服利古里亚以前，当地可能属于斯塔蒂利人。

公元前109年，罗马人修通连接托尔托纳与瓦多利古雷的埃米利娅·斯考里大道，并在卡伊罗设置卡纳利库姆或卡拉尼科驿站。地名源自利古里亚语中表示岩石的词根。

967年，奥托一世把曾遭伦巴德人和撒拉森人袭扰的土地授予贵族，文献中首次出现“卡里乌姆”。当地城堡后来售予热那亚，河谷继续成为地方领主争夺的通道。1796年，上蒙泰诺泰成为拿破仑意大利战役首场胜利的地点，这场战役使城镇获得了更广泛的军事身份。

english: Cais lies near the river of the same name in the Poti basin, rising in the Serra Grande and joining the Poti near the end of its canyon. The Poti cuts through the Ibiapaba uplands between sandstone walls, their surfaces bearing traces of earlier inhabitants. Paintings survive in shelters above the river, while engravings were cut into dark rock beside the water.
simp_chinese: 卡伊斯位于波蒂河流域，附近有一条同名河流，发源于大山脉，在波蒂峡谷末端附近汇入波蒂河。波蒂河穿过伊比亚帕巴高地，两岸砂岩峭壁留有早期居民的痕迹：河上方的岩棚中保存着绘画，水边的深色岩石上则刻有图案。

english: Caisaboscai lies near the Opinaca River, east of James Bay, among lakes and boreal forest. Cree families have travelled the Opinaca and Eastmain rivers and their tributaries for hunting, fishing and trapping. Near the mouth of the Eastmain, a trading post established in 1690 was eventually followed by a permanent post on the coast in 1723.
simp_chinese: 凯萨博斯卡位于詹姆斯湾以东、奥皮纳卡河附近，周围是湖泊与北方森林。克里家庭沿奥皮纳卡河、东梅恩河及其支流往来，在这些水域狩猎、捕鱼和设陷阱。东梅恩河口附近于1690年建立贸易站，1723年又在海岸设立了常设站点。

english: The Cajas mountains rise west of Cuenca in the southern Ecuadorian Andes. Their cold páramo grasslands surround numerous lakes set in high valleys shaped by glaciers. Streams drain from the wet uplands toward both sides of the continental divide. An Inca road crossed this difficult country, linking Tomebamba in the highlands with the route toward the coast and the lodging place at Paredones.
simp_chinese: 卡哈斯山脉耸立在厄瓜多尔南部安第斯、昆卡以西。寒冷的帕拉莫草地环绕着众多湖泊，它们坐落在冰川塑造的高山谷地中。溪流从湿润高地流向分水岭两侧。一条印加道路穿越这片险峻地带，连接高地的托梅班巴与通往海岸及帕雷多内斯驿站的路线。

english: Caka lies beside a salt lake on the high plateau west of Qinghai Lake. Its shallow basin holds a great deposit of salt, produced as water evaporates in the dry climate. The Qing government organised large-scale salt extraction here from 1763, making the lake a source of a valuable commodity in the country between Qinghai Lake and the Qaidam Basin.
simp_chinese: 茶卡位于青海湖以西的高原盐湖之畔。干燥气候使湖水蒸发，浅盆地中形成丰富盐层。清朝自1763年起在此组织大规模采盐，使这座湖成为青海湖与柴达木盆地之间重要商品的产地。

english:
Chaka Salt Lake lies near the eastern end of the Qaidam Basin in Amdo, about 3,060 metres above the sea. Its shallow, oval basin holds a thick layer of sodium-rich salt close to the water surface. In Tibetan, Chaka means simply “salt lake,” while the Mongolian name Dabsun Nur carries the same meaning. Streams and groundwater feed the basin, but arid winds and strong evaporation leave the water highly saline. The flat salt crust reflects the open plateau sky and often appears as a white surface beneath a bright blue vault.

The lake lay within a highland world of pastoral herders, monasteries and routes crossing the Qaidam. Salt was gathered from its crust and carried by pack animals toward settlements and grazing grounds. The mineral was essential for preserving food and feeding livestock, giving the lake a value that did not depend on abundant farmland or timber. Seasonal labour and transport joined the salt flats to the wider Tibetan and Mongol economy.

Settlement beside the lake served the extraction work through a landscape of extreme cold, dry air and short growing seasons. The lake remained a natural storehouse whose value depended on water balance and an accessible crust. Its position near the eastern Qaidam made it a stopping place between the high basin and the routes toward Xining.
simp_chinese:
茶卡盐湖位于安多地区柴达木盆地东端附近，湖面海拔约三千零六十米。浅缓的椭圆形盆地中，富含钠盐的盐层贴近水面。藏语“茶卡”意为盐湖，蒙古语名称达布逊淖尔也有相同含义。溪流和地下水补给盆地，但干旱季风与强烈蒸发令湖水保持很高盐度。平坦盐壳映出高原天空，白色湖面与蓝色天穹常常相互照映。

盐湖处于牧民、寺院和穿越柴达木道路共同构成的高原世界中。人们从盐壳采盐，再由驮畜运往聚落和牧场。盐既能保存食物，也能供给牲畜，因此湖泊的价值并不依赖肥沃农田或丰富木材。季节性劳动与运输把盐滩同更广阔的藏族、蒙古族经济联系起来。

湖边聚落因采盐而形成，周围则是严寒、干燥和作物生长期短促的环境。盐湖像一座天然仓廪，其价值取决于水量平衡和能否接近盐层。这里靠近柴达木东部，因而成为高盆地与通往西宁道路之间的停歇点。

english:
Čakovec grew around a castle in Međimurje, the fertile land between the Mura and Drava rivers. In 1546 King Ferdinand granted the estate to Nikola Zrinski, whose family made the castle its principal seat. The Zrinskis fortified their lands against Ottoman attack and developed trade in wine, livestock and other produce.

The later Nikola Zrinski, soldier and poet, lived at Čakovec from 1637 and wrote his epic on the siege of Szigetvár here, commemorating the defence led by his ancestor. His family maintained a network of frontier posts along the Mura. The Ottoman destruction of their fort at Novi Zrin in 1664 and the subsequent Peace of Vasvár intensified their conflict with the Habsburg court. Nikola died later that year after a hunting accident near Čakovec.
simp_chinese:
查科韦茨兴起于梅吉穆列的一座城堡周围，这片肥沃土地位于穆拉河与德拉瓦河之间。1546年，斐迪南国王将领地赐给尼古拉·兹林斯基，其家族以城堡为主要驻地。兹林斯基家族加固领地以抵御奥斯曼袭击，并发展葡萄酒、牲畜及其他物产的贸易。

后来的尼古拉·兹林斯基既是军人也是诗人，自1637年起住在查科韦茨。他在此写成关于锡盖特堡围城的史诗，纪念祖先领导的防御战。家族沿穆拉河维持一系列边防哨所。1664年，奥斯曼军摧毁新兹林要塞，随后签订的《沃什堡和约》加剧了家族与哈布斯堡宫廷的矛盾。同年晚些时候，尼古拉在查科韦茨附近狩猎时遇险身亡。

english:
Calabar stands among the rivers and creeks of the Cross River estuary, where the Efik built trading settlements in reach of ships from the Atlantic. Known to Europeans as Old Calabar, its communities included Creek Town, Old Town and Duke Town. The port became a major outlet for captives taken from the interior, and its prosperity was closely bound to the Atlantic slave trade. Efik merchant families traded with ships anchored in the river, drawing on connections that extended through the surrounding country and across the ocean.

Efik merchants and European captains competed and bargained for control of this commerce. In 1767 a dispute between trading communities ended in a massacre when British slave-ship crews intervened against Old Town. The struggle strengthened rival families, including merchants of Creek Town and Duke Town. Among the latter was Antera Duke, whose surviving diary records trade, ceremonies and daily life in the late eighteenth century.

Britain prohibited its own slave trade in 1807, but ships of other nations continued to visit the coast. In 1815 the British naval vessel HMS Comus entered Duke Town and seized seven Spanish and Portuguese slave ships. The traffic in enslaved people had already connected Calabar to distant Atlantic societies, at terrible human cost to the people forced aboard those vessels.
simp_chinese:
卡拉巴尔坐落在克罗斯河口纵横交错的河流与水道之间，埃菲克人在这里建立贸易聚落，大西洋船只能够抵达。欧洲人称这里为旧卡拉巴尔，当地社群包括克里克镇、旧镇和杜克镇。港口成为内陆俘虏被运往海外的重要出口，其繁荣与大西洋奴隶贸易紧密相连。埃菲克商人家族与停泊在河上的船只交易，其关系网延伸到周边地区和大洋彼岸。

埃菲克商人与欧洲船长围绕商业控制权展开竞争和谈判。1767年，贸易社群之间的争端以一场屠杀告终：英国奴隶船船员介入，攻击旧镇一方。这场冲突增强了对立家族的势力，其中包括克里克镇和杜克镇的商人。杜克镇的安特拉·杜克留下日记，记载了十八世纪末的贸易、仪式与日常生活。

英国于1807年禁止本国奴隶贸易，但其他国家的船只仍来到这片海岸。1815年，英国军舰“科穆斯”号驶入杜克镇，扣押了七艘西班牙和葡萄牙奴隶船。被奴役者的贩运早已把卡拉巴尔与遥远的大西洋社会联系起来，而被迫登船的人们为此付出了惨重代价。

english: Calafat stands on the northern bank of the Danube opposite Vidin. Its position made it a crossing between Oltenia and the lands south of the river, reached for centuries by boats and ferries. The name has been associated with a place where ships were caulked or tarred, fitting for a settlement whose life was closely tied to the great river. A small Greek community was present here from the late Middle Ages.
simp_chinese: 卡拉法特位于多瑙河北岸，与维丁隔河相望。这里是奥尔泰尼亚通往河以南地区的渡口，数百年来人们乘船或渡轮往返两岸。其地名被认为与修补、涂沥青的船坞有关，与这座依大河而生的聚落颇为相称。中世纪晚期，此地已有一个小型希腊人社群。

english: Calahorra stands above the Ebro valley, a city whose history reaches back to Roman times. Its cathedral lies near the river at a site associated with the martyrs Emeterius and Celedonius. After the Christian conquest in 1045 an earlier church was restored, and work on a new cathedral began in 1484. Construction continued for more than two centuries, so its chapels and furnishings reflect successive artistic styles. Castilian kings repeatedly confirmed the privileges of the city through the later Middle Ages.
simp_chinese: 卡拉奥拉坐落在埃布罗河谷上方，其历史可追溯至罗马时代。大教堂靠近河流，地点与殉道者埃梅特里乌斯和塞莱多尼乌斯的传说有关。1045年基督徒征服此地后，旧教堂得到修复；1484年人们开始建造新大教堂。工程持续两百余年，礼拜堂和装饰展现出不同时期的艺术风格。中世纪晚期，卡斯蒂利亚国王多次确认这座城市的特权。

english:
Calais lies across the narrowest part of the Channel from England. Its harbour and fortified town made it a prized gateway between the island and the continent, useful for merchants and armies alike. For over two centuries Calais and a surrounding district remained an English possession on French soil.

Edward III captured the town in 1347 after a long siege and encouraged English settlers to establish themselves there. Calais became the staple through which English wool was sold to continental merchants, especially buyers from the cloth towns of Flanders. A mint established in 1363 turned proceeds of the trade into English coin, helping supply the garrison and the Crown. Its merchants also helped finance the town's defences. The English held Calais long after losing their other conquests in France. In 1558 a French army under Francis, Duke of Guise, captured it, ending English rule. The loss deprived England of a continental stronghold that had been a base for trade, diplomacy and military expeditions since the reign of Edward III.
simp_chinese:
加来隔着英吉利海峡最狭窄的水域与英格兰相望。港口与设防城镇使它成为岛屿与欧洲大陆之间的宝贵门户，商人与军队都能从中受益。两个多世纪里，加来及其周边地区一直是法国土地上的英格兰属地。

1347年，爱德华三世经过长期围攻夺取城市，并鼓励英格兰移民在此定居。加来成为英格兰羊毛向大陆商人出售的指定市场，买家尤以佛兰德织布城镇的商人为多。1363年设立的铸币厂将贸易收入铸成英格兰货币，帮助供养守军和王室；商人也参与了城市防御的筹资。英格兰失去在法国的其他征服地之后，仍长期守住加来。1558年，吉斯公爵弗朗索瓦率领法军夺取城市，结束了英格兰统治。英格兰因此失去了这处大陆据点：自爱德华三世时代起，它就是贸易、外交和军事远征的基地。

english: Calamarca stands on the high Bolivian plateau south of La Paz, in the country of the Aymara-speaking Paka Jaqi. Its church preserves a celebrated group of colonial paintings of angels dressed as soldiers and bearing firearms. These figures belong to the artistic world of the southern Andes, where European Christian images were transformed by local workshops and patrons.
simp_chinese: 卡拉马尔卡位于拉巴斯以南的玻利维亚高原，是讲艾马拉语的帕卡哈基人的土地。当地教堂保存着一组著名殖民时期绘画：天使身着士兵服饰，手持火枪。这些形象属于南安第斯的艺术世界，欧洲基督教图像在当地工坊与赞助者手中获得新的面貌。

english:
Calamarí was an Indigenous settlement on the sheltered Caribbean bay where Cartagena de Indias later rose. Its shores and islands lay close to routes into the Magdalena basin, while the bay offered anchorage protected from the open sea. The people of the coast possessed gold ornaments that attracted the attention of the first Spanish expeditions.

Pedro de Heredia encountered resistance when he reached Calamarí and founded Cartagena in 1533 on the site of the Indigenous settlement. The new port became a vital link in Spanish Atlantic commerce, including the forced transportation of enslaved Africans. Its wealth invited attacks: Francis Drake captured and ransomed the city in 1586. The Spanish crown responded by strengthening its defences. In 1610 Cartagena also became the seat of an Inquisition tribunal, extending its jurisdiction over a large part of the Spanish Caribbean.

Walls and forts came to guard the town and the narrow channels leading into the bay. In 1741 a large British expedition under Edward Vernon attacked Cartagena but failed to take it. Its fortifications and harbour made the city a principal Caribbean stronghold of New Granada, while the older name Calamarí recalled the settlement that preceded the Spanish port. During the independence struggle, the state of Cartagena prohibited the import of enslaved people in its 1812 constitution; royalist forces reconquered the city in 1815.
simp_chinese:
卡拉马里是加勒比海一座受庇护海湾上的原住民聚落，后来卡塔赫纳在此兴起。海岸和岛屿靠近通往马格达莱纳河流域的道路，海湾则为船只提供避开外海的锚地。沿海居民拥有的金饰吸引了最早的西班牙远征队。

佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚抵达卡拉马里时遭到抵抗，1533年在原住民聚落所在地建立卡塔赫纳。新港成为西班牙大西洋贸易的重要环节，也包括对非洲人的强制贩运。财富招来攻击：1586年弗朗西斯·德雷克攻占城市并索取赎金。西班牙王室随后加强防御。1610年，卡塔赫纳还设立宗教裁判所，对西班牙加勒比地区广大地域行使管辖权。

城墙和堡垒逐渐守卫城区与进入海湾的狭窄水道。1741年，爱德华·弗农率领的大规模英国远征进攻卡塔赫纳，却未能攻克。港湾和防御工事使其成为新格拉纳达重要的加勒比据点，而卡拉马里的旧名仍提醒人们，西班牙港口之前这里已有聚落。独立斗争期间，卡塔赫纳州的1812年宪法禁止输入奴隶；1815年王党军重新征服城市。

english: In northern Sumatra, the country around Calang rises inland from Aceh's western coast. Rivers descend from forested mountains towards the Indian Ocean, while the Aceh court lay to the northeast at Kutaraja. In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the sultanate became a major power, competing with Johor and Portuguese Malacca over the pepper trade.
simp_chinese: 在苏门答腊北部，遮浪周围地势从亚齐西岸向内陆升高。河流从森林山地流向印度洋，亚齐宫廷则位于东北方的库塔拉惹。16至17世纪，苏丹国成为重要强权，与柔佛及葡萄牙马六甲争夺胡椒贸易。

english: The Calansho Desert forms part of the Sahara in eastern Libya. Rock dominates its northern and central reaches, while to the east the desert joins the Great Sand Sea and to the south it contains the Calansho Sand Sea. The contrast between stony ground and great expanses of dunes marks this exceptionally dry country.
simp_chinese: 卡兰绍沙漠是利比亚东部撒哈拉沙漠的一部分。北部和中部以岩石地表为主，东面与大沙海相连，南面则包含卡兰绍沙海。石地与绵延沙丘交替，构成这片极为干旱的荒漠。

english: The Calansho Sand Sea fills a vast tract of Cyrenaica's Kufra District in eastern Libya. This erg, an area of actively shifting dunes, covers approximately 62,000 square kilometres. Its sands extend about 500 kilometres from the Jaghbub and Jalo area in the north toward Kufra in the south. The erg runs parallel to the Great Sand Sea and joins that neighbouring field at their northern ends, so the two should be understood as adjacent but distinct sand countries. Wind has built dunes up to 110 metres high, arranged in rough north–south lines. In such terrain, distance is deceptive and landmarks can move. Caravans followed wells and firm ground around the dune fields.
simp_chinese: 卡兰肖沙海位于利比亚东部昔兰尼加的库夫拉区，是一片由不断移动的沙丘组成的广袤沙海，面积约六万二千平方公里。沙丘从北部贾格布卜与贾洛一带向南部库夫拉延伸约五百公里，并与大沙海平行；两片沙海在北部相接，因此彼此相邻而各具地貌范围。风力塑造出高可达110米、大致南北排列的沙丘。在这样的环境里，距离容易误判，地标也会移动。商队沿着水井和坚实地面绕过沙丘区行进。

english:
Calatañazor rises above the valley in the uplands of Soria, its hilltop castle and walls guarding a small Castilian town. Local tradition places a battle against Almanzor in the valley in 1002; the story belongs to the town’s historical memory, though the battle itself is disputed.

The principal surviving fortifications date to the fourteenth century, when the castle served the crown and was a stronghold of María de Molina. Calatañazor was the head of a community of town and surrounding lands. Henry II of Castile granted its lordship to Juan Fernández de Padilla, whose family made the castle their seat. A ditch protected the more vulnerable side of the fortress, while the steep slopes above the valley supplied a natural defence. The castle’s walls and the town’s enclosed streets preserve the imprint of the lordship that governed the countryside around it.
simp_chinese:
卡拉塔尼亚索尔耸立在索里亚高地的谷地之上，山顶城堡和城墙守护着这座卡斯蒂利亚小城。地方传说称1002年此处发生过对抗曼苏尔的战役；这段故事属于当地的历史记忆，战役本身则存在争议。

现存主要防御设施形成于十四世纪，当时城堡属于王室，也是玛丽亚·德·莫利纳在索里亚的据点。卡拉塔尼亚索尔还是城镇及周边属地共同体的中心。卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克二世将此地领主权授予胡安·费尔南德斯·德·帕迪利亚，其家族以城堡为居所。堡垒较易受攻的一侧有壕沟防护，谷地上方的陡坡则提供天然屏障。城墙与围合的街道，仍留有统辖周围乡村的领主制度的印记。

english:
Calatayud lies on the Jalón in Aragón, between the central Spanish meseta and the Ebro valley. The medieval town grew around a Muslim fortress whose Arabic name, Qalʿat Ayyub, gave Calatayud its name. Alfonso I of Aragón conquered it in 1119. A Jewish community already established by the eleventh century remained after the conquest until the expulsion of 1492.

The collegiate church of Santa María stands on a former mosque site. Its fifteenth-century Mudéjar bell tower and Renaissance doorway added in 1528 show different phases of the city's architectural history. During the Peninsular War, guerrillas took French-occupied Calatayud in 1811; the town briefly became a provincial capital in 1822–1823.
simp_chinese:
卡拉塔尤位于阿拉贡的哈隆河畔，处在西班牙中部梅塞塔高原与埃布罗河谷之间。中世纪城镇围绕穆斯林堡垒发展，其阿拉伯语名称“卡拉特·阿尤布”演变为卡拉塔尤。阿拉贡国王阿方索一世于1119年征服此城。十一世纪已有的犹太社群在征服后继续存在，直到1492年遭驱逐。

圣玛丽亚协同教堂建在原清真寺址上，十五世纪的穆德哈尔式钟楼与1528年增建的文艺复兴式入口，反映了城市建筑的不同阶段。半岛战争期间，游击队于1811年攻占由法军占据的卡拉塔尤；1822至1823年，这里短暂成为省会。

english: Calatrava la Vieja stands beside the Guadiana, its walls enclosing the remains of a fortress that once guarded the road between Toledo and Córdoba. The military Order of Calatrava took its name from this stronghold, which passed repeatedly between Muslim and Christian rulers. After the Christian victory of 1212 the order established its principal seat at Calatrava la Nueva farther south. The older fortress remained the centre of a commandery, though its former importance had passed to the new castle.
simp_chinese: 旧卡拉特拉瓦坐落在瓜迪亚纳河畔，城墙围绕的要塞曾守卫托莱多与科尔多瓦之间的道路。卡拉特拉瓦军事骑士团以这座要塞为名；堡垒也曾在穆斯林与基督教统治者之间多次易手。1212年基督徒获胜后，骑士团将主要驻地设在更南方的新卡拉特拉瓦。旧堡仍是辖区中心，但昔日的重要地位已转移到新城堡。

english:
The Calau country lies west of Cottbus, where Lower Lusatia opens toward the southern edge of the Spree Forest. Calowe first appears in written records in 1279; its old Sorbian root means swamp or bog, fitting ground threaded by wet woodland and small waterways. The town occupied a useful place on the Salt Road that carried salt from Halle across Lusatia and onward toward Poland.

In 1367 Emperor Charles IV bought Lower Lusatia and joined it to the Bohemian Crown, and it passed to the Luxembourg, Jagiellon and, from 1526, Habsburg kings. The Protestant Reformation won most of its people. Under the Peace of Prague in 1635 Ferdinand II gave the Lusatias to Saxony, and Prussia annexed the town in 1815. Calau's people spoke Lower Sorbian as well as German. Its position made it a meeting point between open farmland, wet woodland and higher forested ridges, so the surrounding routes and habitats change within a short distance.
simp_chinese:
卡劳位于科特布斯以西，下卢萨蒂亚向施普雷林森林南缘展开之处。1279年，当地以卡洛韦之名见于记载，古索布语词根意为沼泽或泥泞，符合这里湿润林地与细小水道交织的环境。城镇坐落在从哈勒向卢萨蒂亚、再向波兰运盐的“盐路”上。

1367年，皇帝查理四世买下下卢萨蒂亚，并入波希米亚王冠领地，此后它先后归卢森堡、雅盖隆和（自1526年起）哈布斯堡的国王所有。宗教改革使这里的大多数居民改信新教。1635年，根据《布拉格和约》，斐迪南二世把两个卢萨蒂亚让给萨克森，1815年普鲁士兼并了这座城镇。卡劳的居民除德语外也说下索布语。城镇位置使它成为开阔农地、湿润林地与较高森林山脊之间的交会处，周围道路和生境在短距离内便发生转换。

english: Calbe stands on the Saale at a crossing of the road from Magdeburg towards Leipzig. A royal estate recorded in 936, it passed to the newly established archbishopric of Magdeburg in 968. Archbishop Wichmann granted market and trading privileges around 1160, encouraging the growth of a town beside the river. In the 1360s Archbishop Dietrich of Portitz rebuilt or renewed the castle as a residence, while Calbe expanded and acquired stronger walls and towers. The archbishops used the castle for government as well as residence. The town suffered during the Thirty Years' War, when fighting reached it repeatedly. The Peace of Westphalia assigned the archbishopric's secular lands to Brandenburg, bringing a new ruler to Calbe.
simp_chinese: 卡尔伯坐落在萨勒河畔，马格德堡通往莱比锡的道路在此渡河。它于936年作为王室庄园见于记载，968年转归新建立的马格德堡大主教领。约1160年，维希曼大主教授予市场和贸易特权，促进了河畔城镇的发展。十四世纪六十年代，迪特里希·冯波尔蒂茨大主教重建或更新城堡作为居所，卡尔伯也随之扩展，并修筑更坚固的城墙和塔楼。大主教既在城堡居住，也在此处理政务。三十年战争期间，战事多次波及卡尔伯。威斯特伐利亚和约将大主教领的世俗土地分配给勃兰登堡，卡尔伯由此迎来新的统治者。

english: The Calcasieu River flows south through the forests and prairies of western Louisiana to a broad lake and the Gulf of Mexico. Its name is associated with an Atakapa leader remembered as Crying Eagle. Atakapa communities lived along the river and its lakes, forming one of several groups whose country lay among the waterways of the Louisiana coast. The river descends from the wooded interior into a lowland of marshes and interconnected waters near the sea.
simp_chinese: 卡尔克苏河穿过路易斯安那西部的森林与草原向南流去，经一片宽阔湖泊抵达墨西哥湾。河名与一位被称为“鸣鹰”的阿塔卡帕领袖有关。阿塔卡帕社群生活在河流及湖泊沿岸，是分布于路易斯安那沿海水道的多个群体之一。河水从林木内陆流入低地，在接近海洋之处汇入湿地和相连水域。

english:
Calcasieu Lake spreads through the marshes and cheniers of southwestern Louisiana, where the Calcasieu River meets the coastal system and brackish water mixes with the Gulf. Cypress swamps, prairies, tidal channels and low islands formed a productive but changeable environment. Fish, shellfish, waterfowl and migratory birds were abundant, while flooding and hurricanes repeatedly altered shorelines and routes.

The Katkoc band of the Atakapa lived along the Calcasieu River between the lake and Sabine Lake. They used canoes and seasonal camps to harvest fish, oysters, game and plants from the wetlands. Their trails and waterways connected inland prairies with the coast, and families moved among resource zones rather than remaining fixed around one lake.

French Louisiana brought traders and missionaries into this border country during the eighteenth century. Spain acquired the territory in 1762, and small European settlements appeared near the Calcasieu in the 1780s. Trade in hides, tallow, fish and provisions linked the lake to Gulf markets, while African, Creole and Indigenous communities created a mixed frontier society. The water remained the main road through the marsh.
simp_chinese:
卡尔卡修湖横卧在路易斯安那州西南部沼泽与栎丘之间，卡尔卡修河在此进入沿海水系，半咸水同墨西哥湾交汇。柏树沼泽、草原、潮汐水道和低岛构成富饶却多变的环境，鱼类、贝类、水禽与候鸟繁多，洪水与飓风又反复改变岸线和道路。

阿塔卡帕人的卡特科克支系生活在卡尔卡修河沿岸，范围从湖泊延伸至萨宾湖。他们乘独木舟、设季节营地，在湿地捕鱼、采牡蛎、狩猎并采集植物。步道与水道把内陆草原同海岸相连，家庭在不同资源区之间移动，并未长期固定在一处湖岸。

十八世纪，法属路易斯安那的商人与传教士进入这片边疆。1762年西班牙取得领地，1780年代卡尔卡修附近出现小型欧洲聚落。兽皮、油脂、鱼类与补给品的贸易把湖泊同海湾市场连接起来，非洲、克里奥尔和原住民社群则形成混合边疆社会。水域始终是穿越沼泽的主要道路。

english: Caldera lies on the arid coast of northern Chile, where a sheltered bay opens onto the Pacific west of the Copiapó valley. Its anchorage offers protection along a shoreline otherwise exposed to the ocean. During the 1830s expanding mining in the interior increased the need for a convenient port from which ships could carry mineral cargoes. Desert hills surround the bay, contrasting with the cool and productive waters offshore.
simp_chinese: 卡尔德拉位于智利北部干旱海岸，科皮亚波河谷以西的一处避风海湾面向太平洋。泊地为通常暴露于大洋风浪的海岸提供了遮蔽。十九世纪三十年代，内陆矿业扩张，增加了对便利港口的需求，船只可从那里运走矿产。沙漠丘陵环抱海湾，与近海寒冷而富饶的水域形成对照。

english: Calfuleufú is associated with the stream later called Arroyo Azul, which crosses the pampas south of the Salado River. Its waters run through open grasslands and a landscape of shallow lagoons and seasonal flooding. In 1832 the government of Buenos Aires established a fort and settlement on the stream as its frontier expanded southward. Indigenous communities continued to inhabit the surrounding plains and negotiate with the advancing authorities.
simp_chinese: 卡尔富莱乌富与后来称为阿苏尔溪的水道有关，它穿过萨拉多河以南的潘帕斯草原。溪流流经开阔草地及浅潟湖、季节洪水交织的景观。1832年，布宜诺斯艾利斯政府向南扩展边境，在溪畔建立堡垒和聚落。原住民社群继续居住在周围平原，并与推进的当局协商。

english: West of Cali, the rainforests of the Pacific slope rise into the Farallones of the Western Cordillera. Moist air from the ocean feeds forests on steep mountainsides, while streams descend both toward the Pacific and into the Cauca valley. This landscape ranges from lowland jungle to cloud forest and high páramo. The ridges form a formidable divide between the river valley and the coast.
simp_chinese: 卡利以西，太平洋坡地的雨林向西部山脉的法拉廖内斯山地攀升。来自海洋的湿润气流滋养陡坡上的森林，溪流分别流向太平洋和考卡河谷。这里的景观从低地丛林延伸至云雾森林和高山帕拉莫。山脊在河谷与海岸之间形成险峻的分界。

english: The Farallones de Cali rise above the western side of the Cauca valley, forming a high and steep section of Colombia’s Western Cordillera. Their eastern slopes give rise to rivers including the Cali, Meléndez and Pance, while the western side descends toward the Pacific. Forests cover the mountains beneath the high páramo, and the ridges separate the settled valley from the humid coastal country.
simp_chinese: 卡利法拉廖内斯山地耸立在考卡河谷西侧，是哥伦比亚西部山脉高峻陡峭的一段。东坡发源着卡利河、梅伦德斯河和潘塞河等河流，西坡则向太平洋下降。高山帕拉莫下方覆盖着森林，山脊将有人居住的河谷与湿润海岸地区分隔开来。

english: Calicua is a name recorded among the Indigenous peoples of the country west of the Appalachian ridges. In the northern part of this region, the Monongahela valley supported communities whose villages were arranged around open spaces and whose fields produced maize. Archaeologists have given the name Monongahela to their material culture. These communities traded with other Indigenous peoples, linking the river valleys of the interior to wider networks of exchange before sustained European settlement.
simp_chinese: 卡利夸是文献中阿巴拉契亚山岭以西原住民群体的名称之一。在这片地区北部，莫农加希拉河谷的社群围绕空地布置村落，在田间种植玉米。考古学家以河流名称将他们的物质文化称为莫农加希拉文化。这些社群与其他原住民交换物品，在欧洲人大规模定居之前，内陆河谷便已与更广阔的交换网络相连。

english: The Calicuas appear on early maps of the country west of the Appalachian ridges. Rivers crossing these mountains linked the upper Potomac to the Ohio valley, and Indigenous peoples travelled and traded through the intervening country. Farther north, communities of the Monongahela tradition cultivated maize and lived in villages containing many houses. Their settlements and fields occupied the valleys of a region divided by forested ridges and winding streams.
simp_chinese: 卡利夸斯人出现在描绘阿巴拉契亚山岭以西地区的早期地图上。穿过山地的河流将波托马克河上游与俄亥俄河谷联系起来，原住民在两者之间旅行和贸易。更北方的莫农加希拉文化社群种植玉米，居住在包含许多房屋的村落中。他们的聚落和田地位于河谷之中，森林山岭与蜿蜒的溪流分割着这片地区。

english: The Calima country lies in Colombia’s Western Cordillera above the Cauca valley and the Pacific slope. Its mountains are cut by rivers flowing through humid forest toward the coast. Archaeological remains reveal long-established societies in the region, known for finely worked gold and pottery. Before Spanish conquest, communities cultivated the valleys and exchanged goods across the mountains and adjoining lowlands.
simp_chinese: 卡利马地区位于哥伦比亚西部山脉，俯瞰考卡河谷和太平洋坡地。河流切穿山地，穿过湿润森林流向海岸。考古遗存显示，这里长期存在以精美金工和陶器著称的社会。西班牙征服之前，社群耕种谷地，并在山地与邻近低地之间交换物品。

english:
Calkiní was a principal town of Ah Canul, a Maya province in the northwestern Yucatán Peninsula. Its history is preserved in the Calkiní Codex, a collection of Maya accounts describing the Canul lineage, the boundaries of its lands and the arrival of the Spaniards. Tradition places the founding of the community near a sacred ceiba tree and a well called Halim.

After the fall of Mayapán, members of the Canul lineage established authority in the region. Their descendants faced the Spanish conquest in the sixteenth century. The codex recalls the defeat of the Canul and the tribute presented to Francisco de Montejo near the great ceiba. It also names local rulers and records the settlement of Spaniards, preserving a Maya view of the changes that came with conquest.
simp_chinese:
卡尔基尼是尤卡坦半岛西北部玛雅省份阿卡努尔的主要城镇。它的历史保存在《卡尔基尼绘本》中：这组玛雅文记载描述了卡努尔家族、领地边界和西班牙人的到来。传统认为，社群建立在一棵神圣的木棉树和一口名为哈利姆的井附近。

玛雅潘陷落后，卡努尔家族成员在这一地区建立权威。他们的后裔在十六世纪面对西班牙征服。绘本回忆了卡努尔人的失败，以及在大木棉树旁向弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍交纳的贡品。它还记下当地统治者和西班牙人的定居，为征服带来的变化保存了玛雅人的视角。

english: Callamaco was one of the names given to the Tennessee River on early eighteenth-century maps. West of the mountains, the river bends south into Alabama before turning north again on its long journey to the Ohio. The Sequatchie joins it near the river's passage through the Cumberland Plateau. French mapmakers had earlier used other names, including Caquinampo; by the later eighteenth century the name Tennessee, taken from a Cherokee town, had become established for the river.
simp_chinese: 卡拉马科是十八世纪初地图上田纳西河的一个名称。河流在群山以西向南弯入阿拉巴马，再折向北方，长途流入俄亥俄河。塞夸奇河在田纳西河穿越坎伯兰高原的附近汇入。法国制图者早先曾使用包括卡基南波在内的其他名称；到十八世纪后期，取自切罗基人一个村庄的“田纳西”已成为这条河的通用名称。

english: Callapa lies in the high, dry country of the Pacajes southwest of Lake Titicaca. It was one of the settlements of the Aymara-speaking Paka Jaqi, whose lands stretched across the plateau south of the lake. Under Spanish rule Indigenous people were gathered into colonial towns, while communities retained lands for cultivation and supplied labour and tribute to the new authorities.
simp_chinese: 卡亚帕位于的的喀喀湖西南方帕卡赫斯地区干燥的高地。这里是讲艾马拉语的帕卡哈基人的聚落之一，他们的土地遍及大湖南方的高原。西班牙统治下，原住民被集中到殖民城镇，社群仍保有耕地，并向新当局提供劳役和贡赋。

english: Çallı was a fortified center on the Shumbut in the lands of Volga Bulgaria and later the Kazan khanate. Archaeologists have found remains of surface and semi-subterranean dwellings, a bone-working shop and storage pits from before the Mongol conquest, as well as smithies of the khanate period. Under Kazan it was the center of a subordinate principality and played a part in the khanate's politics. A land inspection of 1619 described the old fortified site as deserted, while recording several neighboring Tatar settlements bearing the name Çallı.
simp_chinese: 察利是舒姆布特河畔的一处设防中心，先后处于伏尔加保加利亚和喀山汗国的土地上。考古学家发现了蒙古征服前的地面和半地穴式住宅、骨器工坊与储藏坑，以及汗国时期的铁匠铺。在喀山统治下，它是附属公国的中心，参与了汗国的政治。1619年的土地勘查将旧城址记为荒地，同时记录了附近数个名为察利的鞑靼聚落。

english: The Caloosahatchee country lies among the marshes and flatwoods of southern Florida, between the Lake Okeechobee basin and the Gulf coast. The river takes its name from the Calusa, whose homeland included the estuaries and shores to the southwest. Skilled hunters and fishers, they travelled inland in dugout canoes, following waterways toward the wetlands of the lake and the Kissimmee River. From coastal villages, Calusa chiefs commanded an extensive network of political and trading relationships.
simp_chinese: 卡卢萨哈奇一带位于佛罗里达南部的沼泽和平地林之间，处在奥基乔比湖盆地与墨西哥湾海岸之间。这条河得名于卡卢萨人，他们的故土包括西南方的河口和海岸。卡卢萨人擅长狩猎与捕鱼，乘独木舟沿水道进入内陆，前往湖区和基西米河的湿地。卡卢萨酋长从沿海村落统领广泛的政治与贸易关系。

english:
Caloto lies in the northern Cauca valley, between the Colombian Andes and the lands of the Nasa people. Spanish conquest brought repeated conflict to this region, where Indigenous communities resisted attempts to impose colonial rule. A settlement was founded in 1543 on the orders of Sebastián de Belalcázar, and its inhabitants later moved the town several times before it reached its lasting site.

Under the name Nueva Segovia de San Esteban de Caloto, the town became a colonial centre for the surrounding valley. Estates and gold production drew on the labour of Indigenous and enslaved African people, while Nasa communities maintained their presence in the nearby mountains. In 1811 Caloto joined the confederation of Cauca valley towns formed against the royalist governor of Popayán, taking part in the political struggles that preceded independence.
simp_chinese:
卡洛托位于考卡河谷北部，介于哥伦比亚安第斯山与纳萨人的土地之间。西班牙征服给这一地区带来反复冲突，原住民社群抵抗殖民统治。1543年，西班牙人奉塞瓦斯蒂安·德贝拉尔卡萨尔之命建立聚落；居民后来多次迁移，才到达长期使用的城址。

城镇以新塞哥维亚圣埃斯特万德卡洛托之名成为周围河谷的殖民中心。庄园和黄金生产使用原住民及被奴役非洲人的劳力，纳萨社群则继续居住在附近山地。1811年，卡洛托加入考卡河谷城镇反对波帕扬保王派总督的联盟，参与了独立前的政治斗争。

sources.title: cali anos de autonomia administrativa pub

english: The Calovébora River reaches the Caribbean coast of Panama from the forested mountains of the isthmus. Its estuary opens onto a shore of beaches and river mouths, with Escudo de Veraguas lying offshore to the west. The river basin drains the northern slopes between Veraguas and Bocas del Toro. Here the Caribbean Sea meets a rugged mainland coast crossed by many short, rain-fed rivers.
simp_chinese: 卡洛韦沃拉河从巴拿马地峡森林覆盖的群山流向加勒比海岸。河口通向沙滩与河口交错的海岸，贝拉瓜斯盾岛位于西侧近海。河流域排干贝拉瓜斯与博卡斯德尔托罗之间的北坡。加勒比海在此接触崎岖的大陆海岸，众多由雨水补给的短河穿过陆地入海。

english: Calpista was one of the Indigenous provinces named in accounts of Hernando de Soto and his passage through Arkansas in 1541. It lay among communities of the interior highlands, between Coligua and Palisema on the route described by the expedition. Salt springs have been suggested as a feature of the country associated with Calpista. The people of the region lived among wooded hills and river valleys, in contact with the larger settlements of the Mississippi lowlands.
simp_chinese: 卡尔皮斯塔是埃尔南多·德索托1541年穿越阿肯色时，其远征记载提到的原住民地区之一。按照远征队的行程，它位于内陆高地的社群之间，在科立瓜与帕利塞马之间。有学者认为这一地区与盐泉有关。当地居民生活在森林丘陵与河谷之间，并与密西西比低地的较大聚落保持联系。

english:
Caltagirone stands on high ground in southeastern Sicily, a town long famed for its pottery. Local clay supplied workshops making vessels, tiles and painted maiolica, whose products travelled beyond the town. The streets and churches occupy a series of slopes, joining the older settlement to the surrounding countryside.

By the sixteenth century many potters worked in Caltagirone, and members of the craft carried their skills to other Sicilian towns, including the town of Burgio in the west of the island. The earthquake of 1693 devastated eastern Sicily and destroyed much of the town and its ceramic work. Rebuilding brought new churches and palaces, while the potters' craft continued to give Caltagirone a distinctive place among the towns of the Val di Noto.
simp_chinese:
卡尔塔吉罗内坐落在西西里东南部高地，长期以陶器闻名。当地黏土供应作坊，工匠制作器皿、瓦片和彩绘锡釉陶器，产品远销镇外。街道与教堂分布在山坡上，把旧聚落与周围乡野连接起来。

十六世纪已有许多陶工在卡尔塔吉罗内工作，工匠也将技艺带往西西里其他城镇，包括岛屿西部的布尔焦。1693年的地震重创西西里东部，摧毁了这里大部分建筑和陶艺作品。重建带来新的教堂与宫殿，而延续下来的陶工技艺使卡尔塔吉罗内在诺托区诸城中独具特色。

english:
Caltanissetta stands in the hills of central Sicily, beneath the ruins of Pietrarossa Castle, overlooking the surrounding countryside of the island. The town grew beyond its old fortified centre as the counts of the Moncada family made it the seat of their power. Churches, new quarters and noble residences gradually spread across the slopes below the castle.

Matteo Moncada acquired Caltanissetta in 1407, and his family retained it until the abolition of feudal rights in 1812. Heavy taxation and disputes with the counts provoked unrest in 1516; the town council later petitioned to return to royal rule. In 1567 much of Pietrarossa Castle collapsed, probably in a landslide. By then the Moncadas had already moved from the old fortress to a residence better suited to their court.
simp_chinese:
卡尔塔尼塞塔坐落在西西里中部丘陵，皮耶特拉罗萨城堡的遗迹俯瞰着城镇与周围乡野。蒙卡达家族的伯爵以此为权力中心，城镇逐渐扩展到旧设防核心之外。教堂、新街区和贵族住宅在城堡下方的山坡上相继出现。

马泰奥·蒙卡达于1407年取得卡尔塔尼塞塔，家族一直持有此地，直到1812年封建权利被废除。沉重税负和与伯爵的争执在1516年引发骚乱，市议会后来请求回归王室直属。1567年，皮耶特拉罗萨城堡大部坍塌，原因可能是山体滑坡。此时蒙卡达家族已经离开旧堡，迁往更适合宫廷生活的宅邸。

english:
Calumbo occupies flat grassland east of Luanda, where the coastal plain opens toward the lower inland roads of western Kongo. Ambundu communities lived across this broad country of scattered fields, pasture and woodland, while the nearby Portuguese port drew Atlantic trade into the interior.

Firm records of a fixed settlement begin in 1836, when Calumbo was a developed river landing. In that year the abolition of the transatlantic slave trade turned attention toward produce and regional exchange. The place grew because goods could move between Luanda and the farming districts beyond it, not because a strong natural fortress or dense town already existed.

The surrounding settlements remained dispersed across level terrain. Cattle, grain and local traffic gave the area value as a threshold between coast and hinterland. Calumbo therefore belonged to a network of routes around the capital before it acquired the municipal form that later maps impose on the landscape.
simp_chinese:
卡伦博位于罗安达以东的平坦草原，沿海平原在这里通向西部刚果王国腹地的道路。安本杜人的社区分布在这片田野、牧场和林地交错的开阔地区，附近的葡萄牙港口则把大西洋贸易引向内地。

关于固定聚落的明确记录始于1836年。当时卡伦博已发展成河运登陆点；跨大西洋奴隶贸易在这一年废止，当地交往逐渐转向农产品和区域交换。它因罗安达与外围农业地区之间的货物流动而成长，并非依靠坚固要塞或稠密城镇兴起。

周边聚落散布在平坦土地上，牛群、粮食和地方运输赋予这一带连接海岸与内陆的价值。卡伦博先是首都外围交通网络中的节点，后来才出现地图上较清晰的市镇形态。

english:
Calvas occupies the southern edge of Loja Province in Ecuador, where the highlands meet the border with Peru. Paltas and Gonzanamá lie to the north, Quilanga and Espíndola to the east, and Sozoranga to the west. The district stretches across valleys, slopes and high ground at an average altitude of about 1,932 metres, in the southern mountain country of Ecuador, where the relief creates distinct settings for settlement and cultivation. Ahuaca Hill, a granite cone rising to about 2,463 metres and formed by two peaks, stands above Cariamanga, the main town, beside a spring.

Before the Spanish, this was the land of the Paltas and the Calvas, who were conquered by the Incas after hard fighting. The Incas valued the district for its mild climate, abundant springs and streams, and the roads that crossed it. In the sixteenth century the Spaniards gathered the people into a mission town, a pueblo de indios, where tribute and labour service could be collected, and Cariamanga became the seat of the Province of Calvas within the Corregimiento of Loja. Early in the seventeenth century, as the local population fell sharply, Cañari families were brought in to supply labour for the mita and the haciendas. By the end of the eighteenth century the place was called the Villa de Cariamanga, and in 1824 the Gran Colombia law of territorial division created the canton of Cariamanga.
simp_chinese:
卡尔瓦斯位于厄瓜多尔洛哈省南部，高地在此与秘鲁边界相接。北面是帕尔塔斯和贡萨纳马，东面是基兰加与埃斯平多拉，西面是索索兰加。这片地区横跨谷地、山坡和高地，平均海拔约一千九百三十二米，处于厄瓜多尔南部山地，起伏地形为聚落与耕作提供不同条件。阿瓦卡山是一座由两座山峰组成的花岗岩锥形山，高约二千四百六十三米，矗立在主要城镇卡里亚曼加之上，山脚有一处泉水。

西班牙人到来之前，这里是帕尔塔人和卡尔瓦斯人的土地，他们在激烈战斗后被印加人征服。印加人看重这一地区温和的气候、丰富的泉水和溪流，以及穿过此地的道路。十六世纪，西班牙人把居民集中到印第安人村镇中，以便征收贡赋和摊派劳役，卡里亚曼加成为洛哈总督辖区内卡尔瓦斯省的所在地。十七世纪初，当地人口锐减，卡尼亚里家庭被迁来，为米塔劳役和庄园提供劳力。到十八世纪末，这里已被称为卡里亚曼加镇，1824年大哥伦比亚的领土划分法设立了卡里亚曼加县。

english: The Calvert River flows north from the sandstone country of the Gulf of Carpentaria to a long tidal estuary. Salt pans and mangroves fringe its lower reaches, where the tide rises and falls by more than two metres. Garawa country extends through the coastal region towards the Calvert and eastwards to Settlement Creek.
simp_chinese: 卡尔弗特河从卡奔塔利亚湾沿岸的砂岩地带向北流去，注入一条狭长的潮汐河口。下游两岸分布着盐沼和红树林，潮差超过两米。加拉瓦人的土地延伸至卡尔弗特河一带，并向东抵达塞特尔门特溪。

english:
Calvi occupies a rocky outcrop above a protected bay on the northwest coast of Corsica, facing the Mediterranean from the ancient province of Cismonte. The citadel stands on a promontory, while the lower town and harbor occupy the shore below. Mountains rise behind, limiting farmland but offering timber, pasture and defensive heights.

The town developed under Pisan and Genoese influence. Its fortified upper town grew around a cathedral and noble houses, and the harbor supported fishing and maritime trade. In 1553 a French and Ottoman fleet besieged and captured Calvi, but Genoa recovered it and strengthened the citadel. Corsican resistance and later French intervention repeatedly challenged Genoese control.

The port exported olive oil, wine, coral and cheese in exchange for grain and manufactured goods. Terraces and groves covered the limited coastal soil. Calvi therefore remained a small but strategic Mediterranean stronghold, its Genoese fortifications and sheltered bay shaping a history far larger than the town's size. Olive terraces and gardens occupied small coastal basins, while ships carried cork, oil and hides between Corsica and Liguria.
simp_chinese:
卡尔维位于科西嘉西北海岸，一处受保护海湾上方的岩丘俯瞰地中海，背靠古代奇斯蒙泰地区。城堡建在岬角，下城与港湾位于岸边，山地从后方升起，限制耕地却提供木材、牧场和防御高地。

城镇在比萨与热那亚影响下发展。设防上城围绕主教座堂和贵族住宅成长，港湾支持捕鱼与海上贸易。1553年法国与奥斯曼联合舰队围攻并占领卡尔维，热那亚后来收复并加固城堡。科西嘉抵抗和法国干预又多次冲击热那亚统治。

港口出口橄榄油、葡萄酒、珊瑚和奶酪，换取谷物与工业品。梯田和果园覆盖有限海岸土壤。卡尔维因此始终是小型却战略重要的地中海据点，热那亚城防与避风湾塑造了远超城镇规模的历史。橄榄梯田和园圃占据小片海岸盆地，船只则在科西嘉与利古里亚之间运输软木、油和兽皮。

english: Calw grew in the Nagold valley of the northern Black Forest around the castle of its counts. First recorded in 1037, it became a trading town known for cloth and leather. Württemberg acquired Calw in 1345, and in the sixteenth century its dukes used the town as a summer residence. Timber floated down the Nagold brought further prosperity in the eighteenth century.
simp_chinese: 卡尔夫坐落在黑森林北部的纳戈尔德河谷，围绕卡尔夫伯爵的城堡发展。它于1037年首次见于记载，后来成为以布匹和皮革贸易著称的城镇。1345年，卡尔夫归属符腾堡；16世纪，符腾堡公爵将此地用作夏季驻地。18世纪，沿纳戈尔德河放运的木材带来了进一步繁荣。

english:
Santiago de Cali lies in the Cauca valley at the foot of Colombia’s Western Cordillera. Rivers descend from the steep Farallones to the fertile valley, and routes over the mountains connect the interior with the Pacific. Indigenous communities inhabited the region before Spanish conquest. Sebastián de Belalcázar founded Cali in 1536, initially north of its present site; it was soon moved to the valley where the city grew.

In the colonial period Cali belonged to the government of Popayán. Nearby gold mines and fertile estates supported its economy, drawing on the labour of enslaved Africans and Indigenous people as well as other workers. The town linked the Cauca valley with Popayán and routes toward the Pacific coast. Its churches, houses and public square formed the centre of a society shaped by landholding, commerce and unequal labour.

The crisis of Spanish rule brought political change to a valley whose towns had developed close ties through their councils, estates and trade routes. In 1810 Cali formed a local junta, and in 1811 its council joined those of Buga, Caloto and other valley towns in a confederation against the royalist governor of Popayán. The prolonged wars that followed disrupted the regional colonial economy throughout the valley but made the city part of the struggle for New Granada’s independence.
simp_chinese:
圣地亚哥德卡利位于哥伦比亚西部山脉脚下的考卡河谷。河流从陡峭的法拉廖内斯山地流入肥沃河谷，翻山道路将内陆与太平洋相连。西班牙征服之前，原住民社群已居住于此。塞瓦斯蒂安·德贝拉尔卡萨尔于1536年建立卡利，最初城址在现址以北，不久迁到后来城市发展的河谷。

殖民时代，卡利属于波帕扬总督辖区。附近金矿和肥沃庄园支撑其经济，使用被奴役非洲人、原住民及其他劳动者的劳力。城镇将考卡河谷与波帕扬及通往太平洋海岸的道路联系起来。教堂、民居与公共广场构成城市中心，土地占有、商业和不平等劳动共同塑造了当地社会。

西班牙统治危机带来政治变化。1810年，卡利成立地方政务委员会；1811年，市议会与布加、卡洛托及其他河谷城镇结成联盟，反对波帕扬的保王派总督。此后的战争扰乱殖民经济，也使卡利卷入新格拉纳达的独立斗争。

sources.title: cali anos de autonomia administrativa pub

english: Cảm Hóa lies among the forested mountains of Bắc Kạn, between the river valleys of Thái Nguyên and the northern frontier. Established as a district in 1490, it formed part of the old Thông Hóa prefecture. Its hills contained mines that drew workers from across the border; in 1739 officials reported that people from China were entering the area to mine without permission, prompting concern over control of the frontier.
simp_chinese: 感化位于北𣴓林木茂密的山区，连绵山岭与河谷地处太原地区和北方边境之间。这里于1490年设县，属于旧时的通化府。山中矿藏吸引了边境另一侧的采矿者；1739年官员报告称，中国人私自进入当地开矿，由于矿场众多、人员往来难以控制，此事引起地方官员对边疆治安和管控的关注。

english: Camacota is associated with Simacota, in the broken mountain country of Santander. The surrounding valleys belonged to Indigenous communities before Spanish colonization and became part of the New Kingdom of Granada. Simacota was established as a colonial settlement in 1703. Its position among the eastern Andean ridges connected local agricultural country with the towns and routes of the Magdalena basin.
simp_chinese: 卡马科塔与桑坦德崎岖山地中的西马科塔有关。西班牙殖民之前，周围谷地属于原住民社群，后来成为新格拉纳达王国的一部分。西马科塔于1703年建立为殖民聚落。它位于安第斯山东部群山之间，将当地农业地区与马格达莱纳河流域的城镇和道路相连。

english:
Camagüey lies inland on the broad plains of central Cuba.
